runs.brief:
A finished run is a decision on the board — the board half of packages/agent-workflows/docs/features.md §8, whose shipped section says what the package gives. Read CLAUDE.md (the apps/web lines), then §8 and its shipped section, apps/api/src/app.ts (`RunDetail`, `onYou`, the list), the Factory (header, cards, "Show finished"), the Runs page's groups, the run page's banner and gate panel, and apps/web/test/e2e/run.ts and seed.ts. You own apps/api and apps/web. Nothing in packages/.
1. Api: `to decide` on the list and the detail as the package words it, with the last step and the command that approves it.
2. Factory: the header counts them (`2 to decide`), and a to-decide card stays on the floor, marked, until decided, whatever "Show finished" says.
3. Runs page: a *To decide* group between *In flight* and *Finished*, newest first, with its count.
4. Run page: the banner says it; the gate panel of an ending step shows the branch's diff stat and the artifacts beside the rendered closeout, with Approve and Send back as they are.
5. e2e: the seed gains a to-decide run and an approved ending; the Factory, Runs and run pages checked in both themes; nothing written that is not taken back.
Done means `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `npm run e2e` green from the root, the PNGs read. End your own servers and watchers before you sign off. Docs: §8's shipped section gains its board half in your words. Every refusal gets a test that makes it refuse at shipped defaults, on `err.message`. Commit as you go, one commit per item, plain messages, no attribution trailers. Sign off by calling the StructuredOutput closeout: `done`, or `blocked` with what you need.

A gate: a step's handoff that waits for a person — packages/agent-workflows/docs/features.md §6, which is the request
in full. Read CLAUDE.md, then §6, then src/workflow.ts (`STEP_KEYS`, `STEP_KEY_MEANINGS`, the parser's refusals),
src/inbox.ts (`INBOX_KEYS`, `INBOX_KEY_MEANINGS`), src/run.ts (`Run`, `assess`, `stepStatus`, `runReady`,
`composeBrief` and its sections — `## From run <id>`, `## Your answer` — `decision`, `listing`, the `wf ls`
vocabulary), src/runner.ts (`start`, `advance` and where a step's dependents are filed, `retry` and the ask files under
`runs/<id>.asks/`, `readAsks`, `cancel`, `forget`/`forgetRefusal`, `parentOf`), src/cli.ts (the verbs, HELP), the README
(the closeout, `wf retry`, "Deciding what ships", the vocabulary table), and test/run.test.ts, test/store.test.ts for
the style. You own packages/agent-workflows (src, tests, README, docs/features.md). Nothing in apps/ — the board's
Approve is a run after you — and nothing in packages/agent-engine. `run.ts` reads no disk; `runner.ts` stays the only
file that imports the engine; `cli.ts` parses, calls, prints; every refusal throws with `.exitCode = 2` and a message
naming the fix; one writer per file.

What to build, one commit each:

1. **`gate: true` on a step**, in `STEP_KEYS` with its meaning: this step's closeout waits for a person before anything
   after it is filed; with `check:`, verified first, then held. **`wf start --gate <step>`**, repeatable, and **`gate:`
   on an inbox card** naming a step (in `INBOX_KEYS`, with its meaning; the board's start passes it through
   `startFromInbox`): both freeze into `gates: string[]` on the record; a step named that the workflow does not have is
   refused at start, naming the steps it has. The `dev-planned*` folders stay ungated (§6 says why).
2. **Held by the tick, level-triggered.** In `assess`, a gated step that has signed off — and passed its check where it
   has one — reads `awaiting approval` until an approval is on disk; nothing after it is ready on any pass, whatever
   the agent wrote. The run's outcome is `blocked`, `onYou` lists the step, `wf ls` says `waiting on you: approve
   <step>`; `runReady` treats a parent at a gate as not shipped. No session runs and no budget is spent while it waits.
3. **`wf approve <run> <step> [--message "<words>"]`** writes `runs/<id>.asks/approve-<step>` beside the retry asks —
   one writer, composed on read — with the time and the words. Refused by name: a step not gated, not signed off yet,
   or already approved; a run cancelled or not there. Sending back is `wf retry <run> <step> --message`, as today: the
   session continues with the objection, signs off again, and the gate holds again; an approval given before the
   send-back is spent by it (the ask's number, as retry asks are spent). `wf cancel` cancels a gated run as any run;
   `wf rm` refuses a run at a gate (something is due to be asked for).
4. **What the next steps are told, and what the screens say.** The approval and its words reach every step after the
   gate as data under `## Approved` in the brief, as `## From run <id>` does, on the pass that files them. `wf decide`
   prints the gate under the step (`approved 23:10Z — "ship the second reading"`, or `awaiting approval` with the
   command to give). The listing's vocabulary gains the word.

Tests that refuse, at shipped defaults: a gated step's dependents never filed without the file, across passes; an
approval for a step that is not gated, not signed off, or already approved refused by name; `--gate` naming no such
step refused at start with nothing written; a send-back spending the approval, the gate holding again after the step
signs off anew; `wf rm` refusing a run at a gate; the brief's `## Approved` section with the words; a parent at a gate
not shipped for `--after`. Keep `assess`, `composeBrief`, `decision` and `listing` pure.

Docs: a README section — the gate, how to set it, approve and send back — the vocabulary table, the closeout's part;
features.md §6 moves to Shipped in your words — built, measured, left — ending with what the board's run should call
(the approve function, its refusals, what a record carries). Commit as you go, with plain messages and no attribution
trailers. Sign off with your closeout: `done`, or `blocked` with what you need.

A plan as a folder of cards: `wf plan <folder>` starts one run per card with their edges, and a run
that waited on runs is handed their closeouts as data. Read CLAUDE.md, then docs/plan-hold-the-bar.md
§4 P ("Cards with edges" — the whole section, including "Then the plan" and what was set aside), then
packages/agent-workflows/src/workflow.ts (how a folder of markdown is read: frontmatter, the closed key
list, `readKeys`, refusals by name, README.md skipped), src/cli.ts (`startHow`, how `--workflows` and
`--repo` resolve, `wf start`'s output), src/runner.ts (`start` and its `after`, `parentRecord`,
`parentsOf`, `advance`'s filing of a gated run's roots and the `baseRef` it reads then), src/run.ts
(`afterRefusal`, `composeBrief` and its `## From <step>` section, `fenced`), packages/agent-workflows/README.md
and docs/features.md (the `--after` section: what it built and what it says is next). You own
packages/agent-workflows (src, tests, README, docs/features.md). Nothing in apps/ (the Factory draws the
edges; P2) and nothing in packages/agent-engine.

Why: a person who describes a plan in prose — A, then B and C, then D — should be able to write it as
files and start it as a whole, with the waiting done by the tick and every card still a decision at
its own `wf decide`. And a run that waited for its parents should know what they concluded, without a
person pasting it.

What to build:

- **A folder of card briefs.** One markdown file per card; the file's name (without `.md`) is the card's
  name. Frontmatter takes exactly two keys — `workflow:`, the workflow to run it on, resolved as `wf start
  --workflows` resolves one (a path, or a name under `<repo>/workflows/`), and `after:`, a comma-separated
  list of card names in the same folder — and refuses any other key by name, as a step's frontmatter does.
  The body is the brief. `README.md` is skipped, as in a workflow folder. Refused before anything is
  started, naming the file and the fix: no `workflow:`; a workflow that does not load (its own refusal,
  prefixed with the card); an `after:` naming a card the folder does not have; a cycle (name it); an
  empty body; a file that is not `.md`; an empty folder. A pure `parsePlan(files)` in a module beside
  workflow.ts, and a pure order (`planOrder`) that puts parents first.
- **`wf plan <folder> --repo <r>`** starts every card in that order with `start()`, each card's `after`
  set to the run ids of its parents' runs — the same record `wf start --after` writes, so the tick, `wf
  ls`, `wf decide` and the board need nothing new — and prints one line per card: its name, its run id,
  its workflow and what it waits on. Nothing else: no plan record (the runs and their `after` are the
  plan), no new store file. If a `start()` refuses midway, the runs already started stand (say which), and
  the refusal is printed with what to do (start the rest by hand with `--after <ids>`). `--after` on the
  command line is refused for `wf plan` (the folder says it). `startHow`'s strictness applies: an unknown
  flag is refused by name.
- **Parents' closeouts as data.** When the pass that files a gated run's roots runs (the parents have
  shipped), each root's brief gains one section per parent, `## From run <id>`: the parent's brief's first
  line, and for each of its terminal steps the closeout `summary` (and the step's declared `output`
  fields, as `## From <step>` prints them), fenced as `composeBrief` fences data. Read off the store and the
  engine's records as `wf decide` reads a closeout (`closeoutReader`); a parent whose closeout cannot be
  read says so in the section rather than failing the filing. Only a run with `after` gets the sections; a
  run with none composes exactly as before. Keep `composeBrief` pure: the sections' data comes in as an
  argument, gathered in runner.ts.

Refusal tests, at shipped defaults, each making the guard refuse: each `parsePlan` refusal above by
name, and a cycle of three; `wf plan` on a folder whose second card's workflow does not load starts
nothing (refused before the first `start()`); the diamond folder starts four runs in parents-first order
with the right `after` ids, and `wf ls` says D waits on B and C; a child's roots, filed once the parents
shipped, carry `## From run <parent>` with the parent's summary (a store test on a real git repository as
the `--after` tests do it); a run without `after` composes no such section; a parent with an unreadable
closeout yields a section that says so, and the roots are still filed. Keep `parsePlan`, `planOrder`
and `composeBrief` pure; `run.ts` reads no disk; `runner.ts` stays the only file that imports the engine;
`cli.ts` parses, calls, prints.

Docs: the README gains `wf plan` (with a four-card example folder) and the `## From run <id>` section in
the brief's anatomy; features.md in your words — what was built, measured, left (the Factory's graph is
P2's; a plan's own page on the board is later). Commit as you go, in small commits with plain messages
and no attribution trailers. Sign off with your closeout: `done`, or `blocked` with what you need.

A run that waits on a run: `wf start --after <runId>`, a pure `runReady` beside `assess`, and `wf ls`
saying `waiting on <run>`. Read CLAUDE.md, then docs/plan-hold-the-bar.md §4 P ("Cards with edges") —
the whole section, including what was set aside — then packages/agent-workflows/src/run.ts (`assess`,
`decision`, `listing`, the `Run` record and its `StepRecord`), src/runner.ts (`start`, `tick`, `advance`,
`isShipped` — what `wf decide` reads to say a result branch is on the base — `list`, `readRun`), src/cli.ts
(`start`'s flags, `ls`), src/workflow.ts (how a key is refused by name) and packages/agent-workflows/README.md.
You own packages/agent-workflows (src, tests, README, docs/features.md). Nothing in apps/ (the Factory
as a graph of cards is the next run) and nothing in packages/agent-engine: a run waiting on a run is the
upper layer's fact.

Why: the sequencing a person did by hand all day — file B once A is on main — as a fact the system holds.
The run boundary is the human gate, so a run's dependents start when the run is **shipped** — its result
branch on the base branch, as `isShipped` already reads for `wf decide` — never when its steps say they are
done. The diamond (A; then B and C together; then D) is then today's flow with the waiting done by the
tick, and every card stays a decision.

What to build:

- `wf start <brief> --workflows <dir> --repo <r> --after <runId> [--after <runId> ...]`: `after: string[]`
  on the run record, frozen at start like the workflow. Refused before anything is written, naming the
  fix: a run id the store does not have; a run on another repository (`repo` differs); the run itself
  (cannot happen — it does not exist yet — but a duplicate id in the list is); a parent already cancelled
  (say so: it will never ship). A run with no `--after` reads exactly as before, and every record written
  before there was an `after` reads as having none.
- A pure `runReady(run, shipped: (runId) => boolean)` in run.ts beside `assess`: true when every run in
  `after` is shipped. The tick files a run's roots only when it is ready — nothing else about the run
  changes: once its roots are filed, the parents are never read again (level-triggered on the way in,
  and a parent's branch deleted after the merge — `wf decide`'s "drop it", or a `git branch -d` after
  shipping — must not un-ready a run that has started; the gate applies to a run with no step filed yet).
  Shipped is read from git each tick, as `isShipped` reads it; nothing is carried between passes. A
  parent whose result branch no longer exists and is not on the base reads as not shipped, and `wf ls`
  says which.
- `wf ls` prints `waiting on <run>` (each parent not yet shipped, by id) on a run whose roots are not
  filed for that reason, in the status column where `pending` would be — and a run waiting on a
  cancelled parent says `waiting on <run> (cancelled)`, since that is a person's to resolve (`wf cancel`
  the child, or start it again without the edge). `wf decide` on such a run says the same and offers
  nothing else. The api's `/api/runs` gets `after` for free if the record is passed through; do not touch
  apps.
- Not in this run: handing a dependent run its parents' closeout summaries as data, and `wf plan
  <folder>`. Say in features.md that they are next.

Refusal tests, at shipped defaults: a run with an unshipped parent files nothing tick after tick, and
`wf ls` says `waiting on <parent>`; the parent's result branch merged onto the base (a real git
repository in a temp dir, as the store tests do it) → the next tick files the roots; a parent merged and
then its branch deleted → still files (on the base is shipped); a parent cancelled → `waiting on <parent>
(cancelled)` and nothing filed; `--after` with an unknown id, a duplicate, another repo's run: refused by
name and nothing written; a legacy record without `after` reads as ready. Keep `assess` and `runReady`
pure; `run.ts` reads no disk; `runner.ts` stays the only file that imports the engine; `cli.ts` parses,
calls, prints.

Docs: the README's `wf start` line and `wf ls` vocabulary, and features.md in your words — what was
built, what was measured, what is left (the Factory's graph of cards, `wf plan`). Commit as you go, in
small commits with plain messages and no attribution trailers. Sign off with your closeout: `done`, or
`blocked` with what you need.

A step that asks gets an answer, and a step that plans: `wf retry --message "<answer>"`, carried into
the try's brief as data, and a `plan` step in a `dev-planned` workflow. Read CLAUDE.md, then
docs/plan-hold-the-bar.md §4 Q ("A step that asks, and a step that plans") and §4b "steering by message
leaves no trace on the run", then packages/agent-workflows/src/cli.ts (`retryHow`, the `retry` case),
src/runner.ts (`retry`, `writeAsk`/`askFile`, and the `e.file` for a try in `advance`), src/run.ts
(`RetryAsk`, `readAsks`/`spentAsks`, `retryRefusal`, `composeBrief` and its `retrySection` — `## Try <n>`
— and `tryNote`/`retryLines`, what `wf ls` and `wf decide` say about a try), and the repository's
workflows/dev/ (README, implement.md, review.md, review.schema.json). You own packages/agent-workflows
(cli, runner, run.ts, tests, README, docs/features.md) and the repository's workflows/. Nothing in apps/
and nothing in packages/agent-engine: the api's answer box is a later run, built on what you leave in
`retry()`'s signature and the ask file.

Why: measured (plan §4 Q), a `--bg` session has no AskUserQuestion and no plan mode. A step that needs a
person already asks the right way — it signs off `outcome: blocked` with the question in `needs`, which
ends the step, is on the record, and is drawn on the board. What is missing is the answer: today a person
answers by cross-session message (no trace on the run) or by `wf retry --nudge`, which continues the
session and tells it what happened but cannot carry what the person said.

What to build:

- `wf retry <runId> <step> [--nudge | --fresh | --model <m>] --message "<answer>"`: the answer rides on
  the `RetryAsk` (`message?: string`) in the person's ask file — the one-writer shape as today; the tick
  honours the ask once, as today, and nothing else is written by the verb. Refused before anything is
  written, naming what to do: an empty message; `--message` with `--recheck` (no session reads it); a
  message on a step that did not end `blocked` is NOT refused — a person may have something to say to a
  step whose check refused, too — but the usage line says what it is for. The try's brief gains
  `## Your answer` inside the `## Try <n>` section (`retrySection`): the message as the person wrote it,
  after "on whose word" and before the check's refusal, so a step that asked reads the answer beside why
  it is back. `wf ls`'s try note and `wf decide`'s retry lines say the try was answered, and `wf decide`
  prints the answer under the step, beside the `needs` it answers — composed on read from the ask file,
  the way the ask itself is, so the run record stays the tick's.
- A `plan` step. The repository gains `workflows/dev-planned/`: `plan.md` (claude, opus, the reviewer's
  fence — `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Skill, WebFetch, WebSearch`, `permissionMode: dontAsk`, the same
  `disallow:` line as review — with `output: plan.schema.json`: `summary`, `files` (paths it would touch,
  with one line each on what changes), `steps` (in order), `risks`; its body says to sign off `done` with
  the plan when the brief reads one way, and `blocked` with the question in `needs` when it admits two
  materially different readings, and that the answer comes back as `## Your answer`), `implement.md` as
  dev's with `after: plan` and `input: plan` (the plan reaches it as `## From plan`, data), `review.md`
  and `review.schema.json` as dev's, and a README that says when to use it (a brief that warrants a look
  before the work, or approval) and when not (a small brief: the plan repeats it). Not the default:
  `workflows/dev` stays as it is. A test loads the folder at shipped defaults and asserts the graph
  (`plan → implement ⇄ review`) and that `plan` has no tool that writes.
- The engine is not touched. If you find the answer needs a field the engine does not carry, stop and
  say so in your closeout rather than adding one: the brief travels as a brief.

Refusal tests, at shipped defaults: an empty `--message` is refused; `--message` with `--recheck` is
refused by name; an ask file with a message the tick honours composes a brief whose `## Try <n>` carries
`## Your answer` with the text and nothing added; an ask without a message composes the brief exactly as
before (no empty section); `wf decide`'s lines for an answered try say so and print the answer;
`readAsks` on a legacy ask file without `message` still reads. Keep `assess` and `composeBrief` pure;
`runner.ts` stays the only file that imports the engine; `cli.ts` parses, calls, prints.

Docs: the package README's `wf retry` line and the usage text in cli.ts gain `--message`; features.md
gains a section in your words — what was built, what was measured, and what is left (the board's answer
box, the steering channel); a CLAUDE.md line only if you hit a trap worth one. Commit as you go, in small
commits with plain messages and no attribution trailers. Sign off with your closeout: `done`, or
`blocked` with what you need — which, for this brief, is the thing you are building.

An inbox: cards parked before they are started — `$WF_ROOT/inbox/`, `wf inbox`, and `wf start` on an inbox
card. Read CLAUDE.md, then packages/agent-workflows/README.md ("A plan as a folder of cards: `wf plan`",
"Files a person gives the run", "Layout"), then src/plan.ts (`Card`, `CARD_KEYS`, `parseCard`,
`cardToStart` — what a card is and how a file is told from a brief), src/runner.ts (`start`: how the record
is built and `runId` names it; `readPlan`, `startPlan`; `readRun`, `listRuns`, `runsDir`, `inputsDir` — the
store's layout under WF_ROOT), src/run.ts (the `Run` type), src/cli.ts (`startHow`, `wf start`'s card path,
HELP), and test/plan.test.ts and test/run.test.ts for the style. You own packages/agent-workflows (src,
tests, README, docs/features.md). Nothing in apps/ and nothing in packages/agent-engine: a second run, filed
after this one, gives the api its routes and the board its page, and it calls what you export — name those
exports in your closeout.

Why: an idea about the project has nowhere to be parked. The right unit already exists — a card: a
workflow, a brief — but a card lives only inside a plan folder, started whole by `wf plan`, or is started by
hand and left where it was. The old hkb filed such a note with `hkb new --triage`, and `hkb ls --phase
triage` was the inbox; its ADR-015 records that triage was a phase pushed into the machinery because a
person needed an inbox. Here an unstarted card is a file in a folder, and the machinery does not change.

What to build, one commit each:

1. **The inbox folder.** `$WF_ROOT/inbox/` (the store's, beside `runs/`), one card per file, in the plan's
   card format with two differences: `workflow:` is optional — an idea often does not know its workflow, and
   it is chosen at start — and `repo:` is an optional key, the absolute path of the repository the idea is
   about, for a board that will one day serve more than one repository. An inbox card has no `after:`: what
   it waits on is said at start. A card with any other key, `workflow:` or `repo:` set to nothing, or a
   `repo:` that is not an absolute path to a directory is refused by name, as a plan's card is. A plan's card
   keeps its rules; a `repo:` on one is refused, since a plan's repository is `wf plan --repo`.
2. **`wf inbox`** lists the cards: name, first line, workflow and repo when set — and `started as <runId>`,
   composed on read, for a card whose name a run record's `from` carries (below). **`wf inbox add "<text>"`**
   or **`wf inbox add <file>`** files one: the name is the slug `runId` makes of the first line, suffix
   included, so two ideas alike do not collide; `--workflow <name>` and `--repo <path>` write the keys.
   **`wf inbox rm <name>`** drops a card without starting it. A name with no card is normal: say so, exit 0.
3. **Starting a card.** One package function the CLI and the api both call — `startFromInbox`, or a
   better name — takes the card's name, an optional brief that replaces the body (a person rewrites the note
   into work at the moment of starting, as hkb let `queue` rewrite it), the workflow folder (the flag, else
   the card's `workflow:`, else refused naming the repository's workflows), the repository (the flag, else
   the card's `repo:`, else the caller's), and `after`; it calls `start()` with `from: { inbox: <name> }` on
   the record, then removes the card. The record is written first, so a removal that fails leaves a card
   `wf inbox` lists as started, never a run with no trace. `wf start <path under the inbox>` goes through
   it; a plan's card is never removed. `wf decide` prints `from inbox card <name>` under the run's line.
4. **Refusals, each with a test that makes it refuse at shipped defaults, on `err.message`:** a key a
   card does not have; `workflow:` or `repo:` set to nothing; a `repo:` that is not an absolute directory;
   `wf inbox add` with no text; `wf inbox rm` or a start naming a card that is not there, saying which are;
   a name that would leave the folder (`../`, a slash); a start with no workflow from the card or the flag.

The pure part — reading a card, composing the listing from cards and records — reads no disk and is
tested like test/plan.test.ts; the I/O sits in runner.ts, which stays the only file that imports the engine;
cli.ts parses, calls, prints; errors say what to do next with `.exitCode = 2`. Tests use a temporary
`WF_ROOT`, as the existing ones do; never touch `~/.agent-workflows`.

Docs: a README section — an inbox is cards before they are started; how to file, list, drop and start
one; `repo:` and what it is for — the Layout section (`inbox/`), and the verb list; features.md gains a
Shipped section in your words — built, measured, left — ending with the exports the api run should call.
Commit as you go, with plain messages and no attribution trailers. Sign off with your closeout: `done`, or
`blocked` with what you need.

Close the fence by machinery: a step may name the tools and commands it must not have, and `wf decide`
prints a finding wherever it points. Read CLAUDE.md, then docs/plan-hold-the-bar.md §4b — "the
reviewer's fence has two holes the brief covers", "what a worker gets, measured", and "`wf decide` prints
a nested `where` as JSON" — then packages/agent-engine/src/facade.ts and engine.ts (how `tools` is
carried on the task) and src/runner.ts + runner-detached.ts (where `--tools` is passed at spawn), then
packages/agent-workflows/src/workflow.ts (`toolsOf`, `STEP_KEYS`), src/runner.ts (every `e.file` for a
step: first filing, try, round) and src/run.ts (`itemLines`, `outputLines`). You own packages/agent-engine
(the task field and its runners, tests, README), packages/agent-workflows (parser, runner, run.ts, tests,
README, features.md), the shipped workflows/ and the repository's workflows/. Nothing in apps/.

What to build:

- `disallow:` on a step: a comma-separated list of Claude Code permission rules — `Bash(npm run build)`,
  `Bash(npm run e2e)`, `SendMessage`, `CronCreate` — carried on the engine's task as `disallowedTools`
  (a field beside `tools`, refused by `e.file` unless a list of non-empty rule strings) and passed to
  Claude Code as `--disallowedTools` on every spawn, by both runners; refused at load on codex, which has
  no tool list, naming `permissionMode` instead; reaching the engine on the first filing, a try and a
  round, as `tools:` does. A rule with a comma inside its parentheses is refused as `tools:` refuses one.
- The shipped `review.md` (dev, dev-build, ui in both copies) gains `disallow: Bash(npm run build),
  Bash(npm run e2e)` — the two commands the project settings must allow for implement's sake — and every
  `implement.md` gains `disallow: SendMessage, CronCreate, CronDelete, RemoteTrigger`, which no step
  needs (measured: a worker has them). The comment that says only the brief keeps review from build and
  e2e is corrected: the fence does.

  the directory behind git's back. A worktree that still holds uncommitted work is committed first under the
  step's name, as the hand-off does — a failed or stopped step's work lives only there (engine open issue 2).

  branch is refused unless a second, explicit flag forces it. Say which branches you kept and why.

  counts — a pass may be filing it at that moment — and so does an unspent ask (`wf retry`, `wf round`

Two keys, neither control flow — one declares, one reads:

- `output: <file>` on a step: a JSON Schema file beside the step, relative to the workflow folder,
  read at `wf start` and frozen on the run record with the step — the folder is a fence the run
  does not re-read, and a schema is part of what the step is judged by. Its properties are merged
  into CLOSEOUT_SCHEMA for that step, and the merged schema stays strict: every property required,
  no additional properties, because Codex enforces strict output schemas. An output schema whose
  properties are not all required, or that names outcome, summary, artifacts or needs, or a file
  that is not there, is refused at load with the fix in the message.
- `input: <step>` on a step: the producer's declared output fields — only those; never its
  summary, needs or artifacts — are appended to this step's brief under `## From <step>`, as data
  and labelled as data. `input:` naming a step this step is not `after` (directly, or through
  `resume`) is refused at load: you cannot read the product of work that has not finished. Nothing
  from any step's closeout reaches a step that did not ask; the anchoring rule stands — the
  implementer's account never reaches the reviewer.
- A producer that declared an output and whose closeout lacks a declared field, or is unreadable,
  is `unsigned` — the existing word: it did not say what it was asked to say — and nothing that
  waits on it is filed.
- `wf decide` prints a step's declared output after its summary, readably: a `findings` array as a
  list, other fields as `name: value`. `wf ls` is unchanged.
- This repository's own workflows: `workflows/review.md` gains `output: review.schema.json`
  (`findings`: an array of objects with `file`, `line`, `what` — what would go wrong — all
  required; an empty array is a review with nothing worth changing) and no longer asks for
  REVIEW.md; `workflows/respond.md` gains `input: review` and answers the findings it is given,
  still writing RESPONSE.md, because a reply is for the person who decides. Then
  `permissionMode: read-only` goes back onto review.md — the reviewer no longer needs to write —
  and the two tests in test/check.test.ts about the review change to say so: the pair is fine now
  because REVIEW.md is not the transport.

findings.what: `Approved` — the panel that stays under a step once its gate is approved — always says "every step after the gate is handed the approval / these words". For an ending step (`workspace: main`) nothing follows the gate: the package hands the words to that step itself (`approvedSection` in run.ts: "A person approved this step before it was filed … their word is what files it"). This is the same wrongness round 1 flagged in the approve box's placeholder one form above, which was fixed with an `acts` flag; `gateWord` got an `ends` flag too, but `Approved` did not, and `runs.$runId.tsx:188` renders it with no way to say which gate it is. The state is in the e2e's own seed: `SHIPPED` has `ship` approved with no words, so its run page reads "every step after the gate is handed the approval" where no step follows it. No test asserts the wording, and the `decide` e2e page never reaches an approved ending.

`AT_GATE` matches a gate line with exactly one send-back and requires the `— or send it back:` clause, but `gateLines` (run.ts:3583) builds that clause from `sendBackTo(step, run)`, which for an unfiled ending step is `step.after`. Two shapes the loader accepts break the match: an ending that waits on nothing (one step with `workspace: main` and `gate: true` — implement confirmed this folder loads when it dropped the send-back form for `back: []`) gives `awaiting approval:  wf approve <run> ship [--message "<words>"]` with no clause at all; a fan-in ending (`ship` after `implement` and `docs`, which `validateMainWorkspace` allows — nothing waits on it and nothing ends beside it) gives `… — or send it back:  wf retry r implement --message "<objection>" or wf retry r docs --message "<objection>"`, and `(wf retry \S+ \S+ --message "<objection>")$` cannot match the joined pair. In both cases `commandsOf` emits neither `approve` nor `send back`, and since `endingMerges` is true it emits no `ship it`/`drop it` either, so the run page's Decide section shows an empty command list for a run whose only remaining action is that approval. `to-decide.test.ts` only exercises an ending with exactly one `after`.

After a send-back at an ending's gate it reads "ship try 2 asked — the next tick files it", naming `ship` for a try that was filed for `review` (`askedSaid` says only "try N", and the `<strong>` above it is `step`). After an approval it reads "approved try 1 — the next tick files what waits on it", where nothing waits on an ending: the approval files the step itself. Gate's default `back = [step]` does not apply to an empty array, so `backName` is 'the work', `to` falls back to the gated step, and the panel shows a "Send the work back" form with no radio group; pressing it posts a retry of the unfiled ending step, which `retryRefusal` refuses with a 409. An ending step's `gate` facts row reads "holds once it has signed off" for the whole of the run before its gate holds, and again after a send-back — visible under `ship` in decide-sent-back-light/dark.png. `standingsOf` puts `git` on `GET /api/runs`, which the Factory and Runs poll every five seconds and which ran none before (the new test proves it). Each finished, succeeded, isolate run whose folder does not merge costs 2-3 `execFileSync` spawns per result branch — `isShipped`'s two `merge-base --is-ancestor`, or one plus `rev-parse` and `rev-list` — in a sequential loop over every run (app.ts:1772), so the api's single event loop is blocked for the sum: 580 ms at 68 branches on the author's own store (RESPONSE.md), growing with the store, with every other request and every SSE session stream waiting behind it. Nothing caps or caches it. Disclosed rather than missed, and the remedies are a design call for a person: one `git for-each-ref --merged`/`--contains` per repository instead of two calls per branch, or an answer cached against the branch tip.

findings.what: `retriesDue` accepts an ask with no message for a step at its gate. `retryable` gives such a step `nudge`/`fresh` through `sendsBack`, but the rule that a send-back needs words lives only in `retryRefusal`, which only the CLI calls. The tick never checks it. A concrete path through the CLI, the one `retriesDue`'s own doc describes: a gated `plan` is running and its harness blocks it, so a person types `wf retry r plan` with no words, which is allowed for a harness-blocked step. The session works again, signs off `done` and settles before a tick stops it. On the next pass `plan` reads `awaiting approval`, `sendsBack` is true, and the wordless `retry-plan-2` is due. The tick files try 2 at once: the session is continued with `status: 'awaiting approval'`, and its brief says a person "sent it back rather than let it go on: what they want changed is below", with nothing below. Nobody read the plan or approved it, `wf ls` never said `approve plan`, and a try is spent. Without the gate the same ask is not due, because an `unverified` step has no modes. A hand-written `{"mode":"nudge"}` file at the gate does the same thing, although the README says hand-written asks are held to the verb's word. Fix: when `sendsBack` holds, count only an ask with `message !== undefined` as due. Add a test where a wordless ask for try n+1 on a step at its gate is not due across passes, and the step stays `awaiting approval`, waiting on you.

The `already approved` refusal assumes nothing has been filed yet. Say `plan` is approved and `implement` and `review` have already run, or a one-step gated run is approved and merged. `wf approve r plan` then says "what waits on it is filed on the next tick, once. To send it back instead, before that tick: wf retry r plan --message …". Both claims are false: nothing is due, and that `wf retry` is refused (`plan signed off done … what waits on it has been filed`). The error sends the person to a command that refuses them. Say the send-back part only while `retryable(...).sendsBack` holds; otherwise say the step has handed on.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the gate change against §6 and checked implement's round-1 replies. Both fixes are right and tested. The won't-fix on `wf tick` printing `failed` holds: every other state that waits on a person prints the same, and `tipBranches` depends on that status. agent-workflows tests pass (517 run: 516 passed, 1 skipped), api tests pass (166), and typecheck is clean in all four packages. One gap remains: the tick does not require words for a send-back, so an ask with no message can send a step back from its gate without anyone reading the step's work. There is also one refusal message that is wrong once a step has handed on.

findings.what: `wf approve` always prints `— the next tick files what waits on it`. That is false for a gated step nothing waits on (`gate: true` or `--gate` on a last step such as review): approving it files nothing, and the run just ends. It is also false when a step after the gate also waits on another step that failed. The refusal text in `approvalRefusal` already tells these cases apart (`steps.some((s) => s.after.includes(name))`); the success line should do the same, e.g. `— nothing waits on it: its run can be decided` for a last step.

'What was measured' still gives agent-workflows as 517 tests (516 passed, 1 skipped). The round-3 fixes added tests, and the suite now runs 520 (519 passed, 1 skipped). A count in a measured section that no longer matches the suite says the section was not re-measured after the last change.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the whole gate change against f866d5e: the `gate: true` key, `--gate` and a card's `gate:` saved on the run record at start, the tick holding a step at its gate, `wf approve`, sending a step back with `wf retry --message`, the `## Approved` brief section, the screens, and cancel, rm and `--after`. Both round-2 fixes hold up: an ask with no words is not filed at a gate, and approving a step that has already handed on now says so. Tests pass: 520 in agent-workflows (519 passed, 1 skipped), plus 217/217 when I ran the gate, run and inbox tests directly; typecheck is clean. I found no correctness bug worth another round, only two small wording and doc errors, listed below.

findings.what: `sendsBack` stays open while the step is approved and none of its dependents is filed. A gated step with no dependents never has one filed, so once approved it can be sent back for ever. Example: gate.test.ts's one-step parent, `start({ gates: ['implement'] })`. After `wf approve` the run succeeds, a person merges it and `decision` says shipped. `wf retry <run> implement --message "…"` is still accepted: `retryRefusal` returns null, the next tick files a new session and spends budget on a finished, merged run, and the run goes back to running, then awaiting approval. An ungated verified step on the same run is refused with `implement is verified: … nothing to try again`. No test covers this: run.test.ts:3082–3087 only tries `plan`, which has dependents. Suggested fix: count an approved step with no dependents as handed on. Add a test where a terminal gated step, once approved, refuses `wf retry --message`.

The gate refusal in `roundAsk` only fires when `budget === undefined`. `wf round <run> review --budget 5` on a looping step waiting at its gate (`again: false`) skips it. It falls through to line 1674, where `satisfiesAfter('awaiting approval')` is false, so the refusal says `round N is still running`. That is wrong: the round has ended and the step is waiting for approval. Without `--budget` the refusal correctly says to approve or send back. Dropping `budget === undefined` from the condition gives the right refusal in both cases.

Low priority, the person's call. A run waiting at its gate makes `wf tick` print `<id>  failed  blocked: implement` on every pass. `assess` counts `awaiting approval` in `stopsFollowers` and reports the run `failed` (run.ts:246), while `wf decide` gives the outcome as `blocked` and says it is waiting on you. A step that signed off blocked gets the same word today. For a gated run, though, this is the normal path, so a person reading tick output sees 'failed' for a run that only needs their approval.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the gate change against f866d5e. It does what §6 and the brief ask: `gate: true`, `--gate` and a card's `gate:` are frozen on the run and refused at start; the hold is level-triggered in `standing`; `wf approve` writes a file per try and a send-back spends it; the next steps get `## Approved`; and `wf ls`, `wf decide`, `wf cancel` and `wf rm` handle a gate. `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass from the root. I found one gap in a refusal: the send-back window never closes for an approved gated step that has nothing after it. I also found a wrong refusal message on `wf round --budget`, and a misleading `wf tick` status word, which is minor.

findings.what: When a `start()` fails part-way, `planStopped` tells the person to run `wf start <plan>/<card>.md --workflows … --after …`. But `wf start` (`cli.ts:256`) uses the whole text of a file as the brief, so a card started this way is not the run `wf plan` would have started. Its brief opens with `---`, `workflow: dev`, `after: b, c`, `---` and then the body. Its run id comes from those lines too: d.md becomes `workflow-dev-after-b-c-show-xxxx` instead of `show-the-flag-…`. And a run waiting on it gets `---` as the parent's first line in its `## From run <id>` section. The printed paths are also unquoted, so a plan folder or repo path with a space breaks the command when pasted. This is the one piece of guidance the brief asked a stopped plan to print, and features.md records the fault as left instead of fixing it. Either make the printed command start the card's body (for example, `wf start` drops the settings block of a brief file that parses as a card), or print something that does, and add a test that runs the printed command and compares the run's brief to the card's body.

reviews.summary: I found one problem, in a rare path, and nothing else worth changing. The change does what was asked: a pure `parsePlan`/`planOrder` in `plan.ts`, a `wf plan` command that checks every card before starting any run and writes the same `after` record `wf start --after` does, and `## From run <id>` sections that a still-pure `composeBrief` puts on a waiting run's first steps. Every refusal and scenario the brief asked for has a test that makes it refuse; the agent-workflows tests pass (340 run, 339 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped as live-only; turbo replayed them from its cache) and `npm run typecheck` is green. The one finding: when a plan stops part-way, the `wf start` commands it prints hand each card's file to `wf start` whole, so the run's brief gets the card's settings lines. `docs/features.md` lists this as left, so it is for a person to weigh rather than worth another round. Two smaller limits are also written down there: a fresh retry of a first step does not get the parents' sections, and the "no plan file" check in the diamond test only counts `runs/`.

findings.what: `afterOf` only matches the bare `--after` token, and `wf start` refuses no argument it does not know. So `wf start b.md --after=a-1x2y` (or a typo, `--afer a-1x2y`) writes a run with no `after`. The next tick files its roots straight away, on a base without a-1x2y's work: silently, the one thing the flag exists to prevent, and the sessions are spent. The sibling verbs refuse this: `decideHow` refuses any flag it does not take, and `retryHow` reads `--message=` and refuses the rest. No test makes `wf start` refuse an `=`-joined or misspelt `--after`.

`parentOf` returns `shipped: false` as soon as any result branch is `gone`, even when that branch's work is on the base. In the diamond, D is gated until the slower of B and C ships. If B is merged and `git worktree remove` + `git branch -d`'d while C is still in review, then after C ships D still reads `waiting on B (wf/B/implement gone)` for ever. B's work is on main, and the only way out is to cancel D and start it again without `--after B`. The request's rule was that a parent whose branch 'no longer exists and is not on the base' reads as not shipped, which implies one that is gone but on the base reads as shipped. features.md:633 gives the reason for not recording the tip as 'the request said shipped is read from git'. That does not hold: `merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> <base>` is still git's answer, and the tip would be the parent's own fact, written by the parent's own tick. No test covers a two-parent child where one parent's branch is deleted before the other parent ships.

'With `wf up` running, the child starts on the pass after the merge, well before anyone gets round to deleting the branch' is false for any child with two or more parents, the diamond's D included. Such a child does not start on the pass after one parent's merge. It waits for the last parent, which can take hours of review, and that is when a person cleans up the first parent's branch. A reader who trusts the sentence deletes merged branches as usual and strands D. It needs correcting whether or not the behaviour changes.

reviews.summary: Round 2 review of `wf start --after`. Both round-1 fixes hold: the gate now says `shipped` only when the parent's own `decision` does, and features.md now says the api builds its responses field by field. Checks pass: agent-workflows 313 passed with 1 skipped, api 89 passed, typecheck clean. Two gaps remain. `wf start` silently drops `--after=<id>` or a misspelt flag, so the run starts at once. A child with two parents never starts if one parent's branch is deleted after its merge while the other parent is still under review, and the README says this cannot happen in practice.

findings.what: `decision` returns `shipped` for any run that is not running and whose result branches are on the base branch, whatever its steps ended as. A result branch is cut at its run's base, so a terminal step that ended failed, blocked or unsigned with nothing committed leaves that branch on the base. `parentOf` asks `decision`, so the gate opens and the next tick files the child's roots, though no person has merged or decided anything. Example: a one-step parent (like the store tests' `oneStep`) whose harness fails before writing, or whose step signs off `blocked` with a question. Its children start, and in a diamond the failure spreads down the graph, each run reading `shipped`. `wf decide` on that parent also prints `shipped — … is already on main` and hides the failure. In the repo's implement → review workflows this needs implement to succeed with no commits and review to fail, so it is rare there. features.md lists it under 'What it leaves', but the README bullet only says 'one that finished with nothing to commit has [shipped] … and its child starts', which reads as the success case. No test makes the gate refuse such a parent. A possible fix in `decision`: count a branch with nothing past `baseRef` as shipped only when the outcome is `succeeded`. That keeps the signed-off, nothing-to-commit parent that the store test ships.

reviews.summary: Reviewed `wf start --after` as it stands after round 3. The last round's three replies hold: the stricter `startHow` refuses unknown, misspelt, empty and repeated flags. A parent's tips are recorded by its own tick, so the diamond's D still starts after B is merged and its branch deleted, and the README now describes this correctly. The agent-workflows suite passes (317 tests, 316 pass, 1 live test skipped) and root `npm run typecheck` exits 0. One problem remains, older than this change and already listed in features.md, for the person to weigh: a parent that failed or blocked with nothing committed counts as shipped, so its children start with nobody having decided.

findings.what: `parentOf` counts a parent as shipped only if every result branch has commits past the parent's `baseRef` (`!isAncestor(b, baseRef)`). That extra condition is not in `wf decide`'s check. Take a parent that has finished (succeeded, every step verified) but whose result branch has no commits past its base, for example a brief that was already done or a step that found nothing to change. Its `wf decide` prints `shipped — wf/p/implement is already on main`, because `decision` calls `isShipped` on a finished run. Meanwhile its child is stuck. `wf ls` shows a plain `waiting on p`, with no bracketed reason and no `→ waiting on you` line. `wf decide <child>` says `nothing of c is filed until p is on main; nothing to decide yet`. `wf start --after p` is accepted instead of refused. Nothing tells the person the child will never start or how to get out. The condition was added so a child would not start the moment the parent's first step was filed, which only matters while the parent is still running. One fix: apply it only to a parent that has not finished. Another: treat a finished parent with no new work as never shipping, with a reason in brackets, an entry in `waitAdvice`, and a refusal in `afterRefusal`. Either way, add a store test where the parent's step signs off with no commit.

It says "`/api/runs` already carries `after`, since the record passes through." That is false. `summarize` (apps/api/src/app.ts:464-486) and `detail` (app.ts:508-534) build the response field by field, and neither includes `after`. The next run, which builds the Factory's graph of cards, reads this list as its brief. It would assume the edge is already in the api and find it missing. Say instead that the api has to add `after` to `RunSummary`/`RunDetail`.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the `wf start --after` change (run.ts, runner.ts, cli.ts, tests, README, features.md) against the brief and plan §4 P. Checks run: agent-workflows tests 312 pass with 1 live test skipped, typecheck exits 0, and api tests 89 pass (turbo replayed a cached result). The gate, the refusals and the frozen record work as asked. I found one correctness gap: a finished parent that committed nothing strands its child with words that contradict the parent's `wf decide`. I also found one false claim in features.md about `/api/runs`.

Both fixes from round 1 hold, and I found nothing else worth changing. `--message` now takes the next argument whatever it starts with. It refuses only when that argument is exactly one of `wf retry`'s own flags, and says to use `--message=<answer>` instead. The answer goes into the brief in a fence longer than any backticks in it, and a test checks the brief's headings with the answer fenced and raw. The rest matches the brief: the answer is stored only on the ask file and read back from it, a try without one gets the same brief as before, the engine is untouched, and dev-planned loads as plan → implement ⇄ review with plan unable to write. Checked: `npm run typecheck` passed; `npm test` passed but turbo replayed all four packages from cache, so I reran the five changed agent-workflows test files directly (189 pass, 0 fail) and apps/api's decision.test.ts (7 pass). One deliberate change from the brief, and it is documented: plan's paragraph field is `approach`, not `summary`, because workflow.ts refuses a declared field named like a closeout's own.

findings.what: `retryHow` refuses any `--message` text that starts with `--`, so an answer about a flag cannot be given. The brief's own example question is "Rename --flag, or keep it?", and `wf retry r-1 implement --message "--flag stays; say so in the README"` exits 2 with "--message takes what to tell the step, quoted". That tells the person to quote something they already quoted, and there is no `--message=<text>` form to fall back on. Only a leading space gets through, and nothing says so. Since `--message` always takes the next argument, take it as given whenever one is there (still refusing a missing one, and an empty one through `messageRefusal`), or accept `--message=<text>`. Then update the test at store.test.ts that expects `['--message', '--fresh']` to be refused.

The answer goes into the brief as raw markdown. Plan §4 Q and the brief say "carried into the try's brief as data", and the package's other data sections (`refusalSection`, `## From <step>`) are fences sized to their content. So a person's text changes the brief's structure. If an answer pastes a snippet and leaves a ``` open, everything after it becomes one code block: `## What the check said` and the closeout contract, which on a nudge are the only instructions left. The step may then end unsigned. A line starting with `## ` reads as a section of the run's. Wrapping the text in a fence sized as `refusalSection` does (still the person's words, marked as theirs) would keep "as they wrote it" and the structure. At least say in features.md that it ships unfenced. Not worth a round alone.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the --message and dev-planned change against the brief. It does what was asked: the answer rides only on the ask file; `## Your answer` sits inside `## Try <n>` after on whose word and before the check's output; a try without a message gets the same brief as before; `wf ls` and `wf decide` read answers off the ask files; and plan cannot write. The four touched package test files pass run directly (187 tests); typecheck and the root `npm test` are green as turbo cache hits. Two findings: `wf retry` refuses an answer that starts with `--`, and says it needs quoting when it was quoted (worth a round); and the answer goes into the brief unfenced, not "as data".

I re-read the inbox change against the request and checked implement's three round-1 fixes, and each holds. `wf start <inbox>/<name>` now starts the card, and a path under the inbox that isn't a card is refused. A relative `workflow:` in a filed file is now written absolute against the file's folder. The `after:` refusal during filing no longer builds a command that names no card. The agent-workflows suite passes (427 tests: 426 passed, 1 skipped, and the removal-failure test ran rather than skipping); typecheck is clean, and each refusal the request lists has a test on `err.message`. The remaining gaps are minor, and the worst of them (two starts of one card at once both start) is already recorded in features.md under what the change leaves.

findings.what: `inboxNameOf` only treats a path as a card when it ends in `.md`, but `wf inbox` and `wf inbox rm` show and take names without `.md`. So `wf start ~/.agent-workflows/inbox/cache-the-views-k2q9 --workflows dev` (the name copied from the list) returns null. No such file exists, so cli.ts takes the path text itself as the brief: `start()` writes and runs a run whose brief is `/home/me/.agent-workflows/inbox/cache-the-views-k2q9`, pays for it, and leaves the card in the inbox. The request says `wf start <path under the inbox>` goes through the start function. Suggested fix: send any path directly in the inbox, with or without `.md`, to `startFromInbox`, so a missing card gets the existing refusal that names the cards there are. Add a test for the path without `.md`. The existing test that asserts `<inbox>/notes.txt` gives null would need to change too.

`wf inbox add <file>` copies the file's own `workflow:` word for word, while cli.ts:445 makes only a `--workflow` flag path absolute. A relative path in the file meant a folder relative to where that file was, as a plan card's path is read from its plan folder. Once the card is in the inbox, `startFromInbox` reads it from the inbox folder instead. Example: a card in `<repo>/plans/` with `workflow: ../workflows/dev` means `<repo>/workflows/dev`. Filed and started, it means `~/.agent-workflows/workflows/dev`, the home workflow store. If a workflow named `dev` exists there, the run silently uses it instead of the repository's. Otherwise the start is refused with a path the person never wrote. Suggested fix: make a path-like `workflow:` from the file absolute against the file's folder when filing, the same way the flag is. Add a test.

The `after:` refusal builds its advice from `file`. When `wf inbox add ./ideas/d.md` hits it, `file` is the path that was given, so the message says `wf start <inbox>/./ideas/d.md --after <runId>`: a command that names no card. What the person needs to do is delete the line, file the idea, then give `--after` when starting the filed card. The test at inbox-store.test.ts:153 only checks the start of the message, so this passes.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the inbox change against 8f792b1. It covers the request: the card format and its refusals, `wf inbox` with add and rm, `startFromInbox`, which writes the record before removing the card, `from` on the record and in `wf decide`, the docs, and the exports named for the api. Existing tests were not weakened, 128 tests in the five touched test files pass when run directly, and the suite and typecheck pass (turbo replayed them from its cache). Three findings: the first can start a run on the wrong brief and is worth one more round; the other two are small.

findings.what: The deny list `Bash(npm run build), Bash(npm run e2e)` matches only those exact words. Two other spellings get through, and the same line is in dev-build and in both copies of ui. (1) `npx turbo run test build` is allowed by `.claude/settings.json`'s `Bash(npx turbo run test:*)`, a prefix rule. turbo.json has a `build` task, so the command runs `apps/web`'s `vite build`, which rewrites `src/routeTree.gen.ts` in the workspace. (2) `node --test apps/web/test/e2e/run.ts` is allowed by `Bash(node --test:*)`. `run.ts` calls `exitOn(main(), …)` at top level, so the command builds the app, starts the servers and writes screenshots into `.e2e/`, since a review session has no `WF_ARTIFACTS`. Neither command matches either deny, so a reviewer in `dontAsk` can run both, and the comment above the line ('the fence keeps review from them, not its brief') is not yet true. Since `.claude/settings.json` is outside what this change owns, either extend the reviewers' `disallow:` with rules that cover these forms, measured as the exact rules were, or keep the comment to what the two rules deny and name the looser allows as left for whoever owns the settings. This comes from reading the settings, `turbo.json` and `run.ts`; I did not run either command, because both write into the workspace.

The line 'A variation the deny does not match is one that allow does not match either, so `dontAsk` denies it all the same' is false at this repository's settings. `npx turbo run test build` (allowed by `Bash(npx turbo run test:*)`) and `node --test apps/web/test/e2e/run.ts` (allowed by `Bash(node --test:*)`) both run the build or the e2e and match neither deny. The reviewer briefs themselves point to those two forms: `npx turbo run test --filter=<package>` and `node --test`. Anyone deciding whether to merge would read this section as the hole being closed. It should name these two remaining ways in, not rule them out.

reviews.summary: The change does what was asked, and implement's three round-1 fixes all hold. `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass from the root, though turbo replayed all four packages from its cache. But the reviewers' new deny list leaves a hole: two commands the settings allow still build the app or run the e2e without matching either deny, and features.md and the reviewers' comments claim the fence is closed. That claim is worth one more round to correct.

findings.what: The new comment ends 'until then the brief keeps review from them', meaning `npx turbo run test build` and `node --test apps/web/test/e2e/run.ts`. The ui brief (the same text in packages/agent-workflows/workflows/ui/review.md:17) never names either one. Only the dev and dev-build briefs gained that sentence, as the package README and features.md correctly say. Worse, the ui brief sends review to the look skill, whose step 2.1 says `npm run build`. That command is now denied, and nothing in the ui brief then stops review from getting the build through the still-allowed `npx turbo run test build`. Either add the dev brief's sentence to both ui briefs, or change the comment to say the ui brief does not cover those two ways in.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the disallow:/disallowedTools change against 9daf925: the engine field, both Claude runners, the parser refusals, all three filings (first, try, round), the shipped folders and placeText all do what was asked, with a refusing test for each, and npm test and npm run typecheck pass from the root. One comment is left over: the two ui review.md copies say their brief keeps review from the other spellings of the build and the e2e, and the ui brief never names them.

findings.what: The comma check is `tools:`'s regex copied, and its quote parts (`"[^"]*,` and `'[^']*,`) fire on a closing quote followed by any later comma. So `disallow: Bash(git commit -m 'wip'), SendMessage` (or the same with double quotes) is refused with "has a comma inside an entry", and the "pieces" it lists are the correct two rules. The same two rules in the other order, `SendMessage, Bash(git commit -m 'wip')`, pass. The engine's `RULE` accepts both. For `tools:` a quote is never valid, so the false match never mattered there; for a rule, a quote inside the parentheses is legal. The quote and bracket parts buy nothing here: `"SendMessage, CronCreate"` and `[SendMessage, CronCreate]` split into entries that already fail `RULE` (they don't start with a letter). Only the parenthesis part is needed. No test has a quoted rule followed by another entry.

The new sentence about `implement`'s deny list was inserted before "Its findings are its closeout (`review.schema.json`), and `again: true` sends the change round again". "Its" now points to implement, so the README says implement's findings are the review schema and implement decides whether to go round again. The same happens in workflows/ui/README.md:18: "It is handed implement's screenshots and pages … reads the diff, and uses the look skill" now follows the implement sentence, so it reads as implement being handed its own screenshots. Name `review` in both sentences.

"Measured, as `--tools` was" isn't accurate. `--tools` was proven on a `claude --bg` session with a control (`test/live.test.ts:70`). `--disallowedTools` was tried once by hand on `claude -p`. Every shipped Claude reviewer runs `harness: claude`, which spawns `claude --bg`, so nothing has shown the deny reaching the harness these steps actually run on. features.md and the review.md comments go further and say "the fence keeps review from them, not its brief". Either measure on `--bg` (an `AE_LIVE` test beside the `--tools` one, with a control) or say the measurement was on `claude -p` only.

reviews.summary: I read the whole diff against 9daf925: the engine field and both runners' spawn args, the `disallow:` parser, the three `e.file` paths (first filing, try, round), `placeText`/`itemLines`, the tests, and the shipped folders and READMEs. `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` are green from the root, replayed from turbo's cache. Everything asked for is there and tested, with one real parser bug: the comma check copied from `tools:` wrongly refuses a valid rule containing a quote when another entry follows it. The other two findings are wording: two README sentences now point at the wrong step, and the README says the deny was measured like `--tools` when it wasn't.

I reviewed the whole engine diff against 2addc61. The fix for last round's finding holds: `measured` is now written once, when a key has a value the record lacks. I found nothing else worth changing. The engine's 307 tests ran directly: 299 passed, 0 failed, and 8 were skipped because they need `AE_LIVE=1`. `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` passed too, but only as turbo cache replays. Two things for whoever merges: `budgetUsd` is refused on `claude`, the harness agent-workflows runs its steps on, because a measured `--bg` session given a $0.01 cap spent $0.19, so no step can be capped yet (issue 17). And a budget end now settles the task with no retry, which the commit says was the operator's call.

findings.what: The check that writes `measured` once only asks whether each key is present (`Object.keys(measured).some(key => !Object.hasOwn(attempt.usage ?? {}, key))`), not whether it has a value. The composite runner always has a `release`: for a harness without one it resolves `undefined` (runner-composite.ts:62-64), so in `createEngine()` this line falls back to `session.usage` for every observed attempt of every harness. Case: a `PromiseRunner` whose `observe` reports `usage: { turns: 3, costUsd: undefined }`. That type-checks, since tsconfig has no `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, and it is the shape `runner-sdk.ts:68` uses with `turns: m.num_turns`. On the default files journal, `JSON.stringify` drops the `undefined` key when the entry is appended, so the key is never on `attempt.usage`. The result: a new `measured` entry for that attempt on every tick while the session is observed, growing the journal and the feed without bound. No shipped harness produces an `undefined` value, so this is latent for API users. Fix: count a key only when `measured[key] !== undefined` and the attempt lacks it, and add a test against `Journal.filesOps` with a runner that reports an `undefined` value, asserting one entry over several passes.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the four engine commits against the brief and found one real bug: the check meant to write a `measured` entry once can instead append one on every tick. `npm test` (all packages) and `npm run typecheck` pass. The implementation covers everything the brief asked for; two measured outcomes need a person's decision: `budgetUsd` is refused on `claude`, the harness agent-workflows runs its steps on (a `--bg` session ignored `--max-budget-usd`), so only `claude-detached` can cap spend; and a session ended on its budget is retried from scratch under the same cap, so `maxAttempts: N` can spend up to N caps on the same brief.

findings.what: Round 1 fixed the agent's brief so it says why the last try ended (`ownStatus`); the person's screen is still missing it. Case: `budget: 3` on a claude step whose session crashes and is settled `failed` after spending $3.40, or one that ends `unsigned` or `stopped`. `decision` (run.ts:1986–1997) files it only under `overBudget`, so `wf decide` no longer prints `FAILED: implement  (wf logs <run> <step>)` or `UNSIGNED: … ended without the closeout`, and the run's outcome changes from `failed` to `blocked`. The offer at run.ts:1076 then reads only `implement: over budget, $3.40 of $3. Raise its cap above $3.40 and continue its session`. The per-step section of cli.ts prints no status word for the step, and the `wf ls` word is `over budget …`. Nothing a person reads says the session broke, or points at its logs, at the moment they decide whether to pay for a nudge of it or a fresh session. The check lines still show a refused check, and `answerLines` still shows a blocked step's question, so only failed, stopped and unsigned are hidden. Fix: carry the step's own status beside the budget word. For example `implement: over budget (failed), $3.40 of $3 …` in `retryLines`, and the OVER BUDGET banner saying why each step stopped, keeping the `wf logs` pointer for a failed one. Add a test that asserts the `failed` and `unsigned` cases on `wf decide`.

The OVER BUDGET banner gives the same reason for every step it lists: `its tries have cost its budget: or more`. In the loop case the tests build (implement $4.25 of $3, review $0.50 and not over), `decision.overBudget` is `['implement', 'review']`. So the banner says review's tries cost its budget, which is false: review is held only because the round would file implement again. Say the looping step is held on another step's budget, as `wf ls` already does (`over budget — implement $4.25 of $3`).

`listing` adds every step whose word is `over budget` to `priced`, and `priced` suppresses that step's `cost` beside the word (run.ts:2096). That is right for a step whose word carries its own amount. It is wrong for a looping step held on another step's budget: `budgetStatus` (run.ts:2153) prints only the other step's amounts. So in the loop test, review's $0.50 appears nowhere on its `wf ls` line, although the run's total counts it. Only skip the `cost` when the word shows this step's own spend (`overBudget(step)` or `budget exhausted`).

reviews.summary: I reviewed the budget and cost change in packages/agent-workflows against the engine README and `src/domain.ts` in this workspace. Its base, 1944644, already has E8 merged, so I did not read the E8 branch. All three round-1 replies hold up in the code and the tests. The agent-workflows suite, the full `npx turbo run test --force` (4/4) and typecheck all pass. One gap is worth another round: on `wf decide`, a step that is over budget no longer says how its last try ended. Two smaller wording and display issues can go in the same round. apps/api still passes no `spendOf`, which features.md already lists as work for the next apps run.

findings.what: For one tick after a person raises a loop's budget with `wf round --budget`, the screens say the run still waits on them. Take implement with `budget: 3` that has spent $4.25, and review asking `again: true` below its `rounds:`. After `wf round r review --budget 10` and before the next tick, `assess` marks only the looping step (review) as `running`. Implement still reads `over budget`, because it is held on review's request for a round, and that status stops what follows, so the run's status is `failed`. The results in that window: (1) `wf decide` reads awaiting/blocked, prints `OVER BUDGET, waiting on you: implement ($4.25 of $3), review (held: …)`, and offers `wf round r review --budget <amount>` again, which `roundAsk` then refuses as already asked. (2) `wf ls` prints `→ waiting on you: implement`, because `listing` only takes out a step whose own name has a round due. (3) The pass that files the round reports `failed`. An exhausted loop asked for with plain `wf round` reads `running` in the same window, because its target reads `verified`. A `wf retry --budget` does not have this problem, since the retried step itself is marked running. The store test (test/store.test.ts:619–622) never looks between the ask and the pass, so nothing catches this. Possible fix: once a round is due for a loop, treat every step in its `loopSpan` as running, or as not held, in both `assess` and `listing`.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the workflow half of cost and budget, with E8 already on main (merge 1944644), so the engine's README and src/domain.ts came from this workspace. Round 2's three findings are fixed and tested: `wf decide` again shows FAILED or UNSIGNED for a step past its budget, the OVER BUDGET line gives each step its own reason, and `wf ls` keeps a held looping step's own cost beside its word. The agent-workflows tests pass without turbo's cache (406 tests: 405 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed), and typecheck is clean in every package; the root `npm test` also passed, but turbo replayed that result from cache. One gap is left for a person: for one tick after `wf round --budget`, the run's screens still say it is waiting on you. Nothing is filed wrongly and nothing extra is spent, so it is not worth another round.

findings.what: `held` treats every `failed (check)` as a way on through another session, including a check that did not finish (killed at its deadline, or stopped). Case: a step over its budget whose check hit its deadline reads `over budget`. `decision` builds `unfinishedCheck` only from `named('failed (check)')` (run.ts:1950), so `wf decide` drops `CHECK DID NOT FINISH` and prints `OVER BUDGET … raise the cap`. `retryLines`' `if (raise)` branch (run.ts:1032) also runs before the `unfinishedCheck` offer, so the person is told to raise a cap. The actual way on is a free `--recheck`, which is exactly the case CLAUDE.md says is not a verdict on the work. `over budget`'s own definition ("another session of it is the way on") does not hold here. No test covers an unfinished check past a budget.

On `claude-detached`, each filing hands the engine the whole cap in force as `budgetUsd`, not the cap minus what the step has already spent. The README says the cap bounds the tries together. Case: `budget: 3`, `retries: 2`. Try 1 costs $2.90 and its check refuses. That is under the cap, so `retries:` files try 2 with `budgetUsd: 3`, and the step can end at $5.90 against a $3 cap, on the one harness that could have stopped it at $3. The same after a raise: `wf retry --budget 10` after $4.25 spent gives the new session $10, so the step can reach $14.25. The README's table warns of a one-try overrun only on `claude`. Either hand `cap − stepSpend` and hold the step when nothing is left, or say in the README that `claude-detached` can overrun by up to a whole cap per try. The same applies to the round filing (runner.ts:1083) and the first filing (runner.ts:1173).

The brief of a person's `--budget` try gets the masked status (`stepStatus` → `over budget`), and `retrySection` (run.ts:2336) picks its `why` sentence by that status. That replaces the sentence saying why the last try actually stopped. Case: an `unsigned` step over its budget, nudged with `wf retry --budget 10`, is only told its tries cost more than the budget. It is never told "The last try ended without the closeout the run asked for" (run.ts:2318), which is what a nudge of an unsigned session exists to say. A `blocked`, `failed` or `stopped` step loses its sentence the same way. A refused check still gets its refusal section. Pass the step's own status (`standing().own`) to the brief, and add the budget sentence beside it rather than instead of it.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the four commits against 1944644. E8 is merged there, so I read the engine's README (budget and cost sections) and `src/domain.ts` from this workspace, not from the eou6 branch. agent-workflows passes 400 tests (399 pass, 1 skipped), apps/api passes 129/129 and typecheck is clean. The change does what was asked: the key and its refusals, `over budget` and `budget exhausted`, `--budget` on `wf retry` and `wf round`, cost on `wf ls`, `wf decide` and the timeline, and the docs. The flaw: `over budget` hides the status underneath, which loses a check that did not finish and blunts the brief of the try a person files, and on `claude-detached` each session gets the whole cap rather than what is left of it.

findings.what: `budget.over` comes from `overBudget` (apps/api/src/app.ts:208). That only asks whether the spend is at or above the cap, not whether the step is held. Take a `claude` step with `budget: 3` whose one `--bg` session cost $3.20: such a session ignores the cap (issue 17), so this overrun will be common. It signs off done and its check passes. The chip reads `verified ✓` and what waits on it runs. But the node's cost row is red `$3.20 of $3`, and hovering it says 'the cap or more, so the run spends nothing more on it until a person raises it', which is false because nothing waits on a raise. The doc on `StepBudget.over` (app.ts:44-48) says the same wrong thing: 'what holds the step, where another session of it is the way on'. Red past the cap is what was asked for, but the hover and the doc should only claim the step is held when its word is `over budget` or `budget exhausted`. No test covers a verified step past its cap; components.test.ts only has a verified step within it.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the change against 60e5606. Both of last round's fixes hold up: the raise row now answers a step that signed off blocked past its budget and offers a recheck, and the banner gives 'past its budget' as a reason. All four packages pass `npx turbo run test --force` and `npm run typecheck`, and I read implement's cost screenshots in both themes. The api's `raiseOf` matches what the package's `retryable`, `roundAsk` and `roundLines` accept. Viewing every earlier try in `viewsOf` looks at no harness for settled tasks, so the decision endpoint does not get slower. One small wording issue is left for a person and is not worth another round.

findings.what: A step that signed off blocked and is over its budget can't be answered from the board. The package's `held` marks a settled blocked step (also an unsigned one, or one whose check refused) `over budget $X of $Y`. `stepState` then reads 'over-budget', not 'blocked', so `offersOf` gives it only a RaiseRow. That row (Decide.tsx `RaiseRow`) has a nudge/fresh choice and an amount, but no message box, and no recheck for a refused check. The banner still shows `<step> asks: <needs>`. Yet the only thing the page offers sends `{mode, budget}` with no answer. The package's own offer for this case is `wf retry <run> <step> --budget <amount> --message "<answer>"` (`answerLines`), and `retryLines` says `--recheck … needs no --budget` for a refused check. Once the raise is asked, try N+1 is taken. A second ask carrying the answer is refused as already asked, so the answer is lost unless someone deletes the ask file by hand. Nothing tests a blocked or unsigned step past its budget: the seed and budget.test.ts cover only a refused check and a held loop. Fix: give RaiseRow a message box (sent as `message`) when the step's own word is blocked or unsigned, and keep the recheck option where the check refused. Add a component test and an api test for a blocked step over its budget.

The run page's banner explains every step waiting on you with a fixed list of reasons: "signed off blocked, unsigned, refused by its check, or out of rounds". This change makes steps over budget, or ended at it, wait on you too, and the list doesn't include them. On the seeded COSTLY run (cost-light.png, cost-dark.png) it reads "Waiting on you: implement, review, tokens — signed off blocked, unsigned, refused by its check, or out of rounds". implement and review did their work and are held only by implement's $2 budget. A person reading the banner gets the wrong reason for all three. The e2e checks only the prefix `Waiting on you: implement, review, tokens`, so it doesn't catch this. Fix: add "or past its budget" and cover it in the e2e assertion.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the four commits against 60e5606: the api routes and fields, the board's components, the tests and the e2e seed. I also looked at the implement step's cost-page screenshots in both themes, plus the runs list in dark and the Factory in light. `npx turbo run test --force` passes in every package and `npm run typecheck` is green. Costs, budgets, the timeline column, the header and card, and the refusals all follow the package's words. Two gaps remain on the run page: a step that stopped for another reason and is also over its budget loses its answer box, and the waiting-on-you banner gives the wrong reasons for steps held on a budget.

Round 2: nothing I would send back. A dragged card now takes along every card that waits on it, the way a dragged step takes along its followers, and the cards it waits on stay put. The 86 web unit tests the change touches pass when run directly, and the full suite replays green from turbo's cache. I judged the pages from implement's screenshots alone, because serving the app and the browser tools are denied in this mode. All 8 screenshots were taken after the last commit with no `-failed` file beside them, and nothing is cut off, overlapping or unreadable in light or dark. Typecheck was not run, since the brief limits turbo to the test task. Both round 1 won't-fixes hold: their reasons stand, the span limit is written on `spanOf` and pinned by a unit test, and the tall-card overlap predates this diff.
