The recheck option closes the message box, and the e2e shows a real 409 word for word beside the box with nothing written. I checked the new POST route against its guard, `messageRefusal`, `retryRefusal`, `answerOf` and `tryNote` and found no correctness bug. The api tests cover each refusal the brief lists. `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass, though turbo replayed both from its cache rather than running them. I read the e2e screenshots from the implement artifacts in both themes: the `held` banner, the node, the refused and accepted answer, and the Factory. They read correctly.

findings.what: The Continue button for a session the harness blocked can never succeed. The engine's `needsHuman` (agent-engine/src/domain.ts:402) needs an attempt that has not ended. `stepStatus` therefore calls the step `running` (run.ts:221), `retryable` gives it no modes, and `retry()` refuses with "implement is still running, so there is nothing to try again until it ends. Wait for it" (409). The api test asserts exactly that for `held`, and the e2e's `held` page deliberately does not press the button. So on HELD a person reads "— continue it" in the banner (runs.$runId.tsx:64) and in the row (Decide.tsx:119), clicks Continue, and gets a red refusal telling them to wait. The hint beside the button, `wf retry <run> implement`, is refused the same way. Plan §4b line 715 already records that `wf retry` cannot help here, and resuming the session is §6 item 10's tick. The brief said to stop and name a package gap rather than work around it. Offer no action the package refuses: say plainly that the board cannot continue this session today, say what a person can do, and name the gap in the closeout.

`offersOf` builds a `continue` offer for every step with `blockedByHarness`, and `runs.$runId.tsx` renders the Decide section for a running run because of that offer alone. The only offer this code gives a harness-blocked step is one the package refuses in every case (see the Decide.tsx:169 finding), and the unit and component tests pin that dead offer as the expected shape (asks.test.ts, components.test.ts). Whatever replaces it should update these tests, not keep them green.

`lastLineOf` calls `e.transcript(taskId)` for every harness-blocked step on every GET /api/runs and GET /api/runs/:id. For an attempt still in flight, which is always the case for `needs-human`, the engine's `transcript` has no `nativeId` and calls `runner.observe`, one `claude agents --json` per call (agent-engine/src/facade.ts:371). The Factory and the run page each poll every 5 s (web lib/api.ts:288, 419), and /api/runs awaits runs one after another (app.ts:1177). The route's own comment at app.ts:1166 still promises "one harness observation" per request. With the two sessions the login race blocked at once (plan §4b, 2026-09-13), each Factory poll makes 3 registry calls instead of 1, about 0.3 s each, the cost the §4b api-tests bullet says kills the api tests under contention. Either read the last line only on the run's own page (the card can say "blocked by the harness" without the line), or fix the comment and accept the cost knowingly.

For a check that did not finish, the row defaults to `recheck` (Decide.tsx:134) and still shows a textarea inviting "Anything to tell it (optional): the next try is told it." Any text typed there is sent with the recheck, and `messageRefusal` always refuses a message on a recheck with a 422. The easiest path through that row is a guaranteed refusal. Disable or hide the box while `recheck` is selected, or drop the message when the mode is recheck.

The brief says a refusal is "shown verbatim beside the box, never swallowed", and no test proves it. components.test.ts only asserts `data-refused` is absent, a server render cannot reach a mutation's error state, and api.test.ts stops at `askTry` rejecting. Rendering `ask.error.message` in OfferRow is unchecked: a change that dropped the `data-refused` block would pass the whole suite. The e2e could make one refused ask through the board (for example, theme with recheck and a message → 422) and assert the package's sentence appears beside the row, with no ask file written.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the change against ed702d7. Suite and typecheck are green, and the implement step's screenshots in both themes show the question on the card, node and banner, the harness line, and `try 2 asked` after an answer. The refusal tests the brief asked for are all there. Two things stop this shipping as asked. The "Continue" offered for a session the harness blocked can never succeed: the package reads such a step as still running and refuses it with a 409, and the e2e avoids pressing it for that reason. And each such step now costs every /api/runs poll an extra `claude agents` call.

findings.what: The ending's gate holds while the loop is going round again. When review signs off `again: true` with rounds left, `ownStatus` reads it `unverified`, so `satisfiesAfter` here is true and `waitsAtGate(ship)` returns true — `atGate` has the matching guard for this case (line 382, `step.loop && again === true`), `waitsAtGate` has none. In the very pass where `assess` returns `round: [review]` it also returns `toDecide: {kind:'approve', step:'ship'}` and `ship: awaiting approval`, so `wf ls` and the board say `→ to decide: Ship it: trial merge … — wf approve <run> ship` at the moment the reviewer asked for the work to be changed; the window lasts until the next tick files the round, and for ever if no `wf up` is running. `approvalRefusal`'s new guard (line 342) only looks for a pending RetryAsk on a step in `after`, and a round asked by `again: true` writes no ask, so the approval is accepted, is written against ship's try 1, and nothing ever spends it (`spentApprovals` needs `try < tryOf`, and the round resets review, not ship). When the extra round finishes, the tick files ship and the merge runs on work whose final review the person never saw. Reachable in every shipped `dev*` folder, since ship waits on the looping review step.

For a run started `--no-worktree` (`isolate: false`), every step's branch is the base branch, so `resultSteps(...).map(branch)` is `['main']` and the ending step's brief reads "The work of review is not in this directory: it is on main, cut from `<sha>`" — false, the work is in that directory — and hands it `git log --oneline main..main` and `git diff main...main`, which print nothing. A session following the shipped `ship.md` then runs `git merge --no-ff --no-commit main` on main (a no-op, exit 0), runs the folder's whole check, has `git commit --no-edit` fail with nothing to commit, and `git merge --abort` fail with no merge in progress, so the ending signs off `blocked` after paying for a full suite run. Nothing refuses the combination, and decide.test.ts builds exactly such a run (`isolate: false` with a `workspace: main` ending) to test the screen, so the path is live and untested for the brief.

`endingSteps` is any terminal gated step, so `wf start --workflows workflows/ui --gate review` makes review an "ending": at its gate the run says `→ to decide: Review the change in this workspace as a second engineer would. — wf approve …` (the step's own instructions, offered as what happens next), and once approved `toDecide` is undefined while `ending.length` is 1, so `wf decide` prints neither the to-decide block nor `ship it`/`drop it`. The branch holding all of that run's work is left with no command anywhere on the screen. §8 justified dropping the git commands for a research ending because that branch "holds nothing"; here it holds everything, and the run has no `workspace: main` step that would merge it.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the whole change against §8: `workspace: main` and its refusals, the ending gate held before filing (`approvedFirst`/`waitsAtGate`), `resultSteps`, `toDecide`/`branchStandings`, `wf decide`'s facts, the four `ship.md` files and the tests. Ran `npm run typecheck` (clean) and `npx turbo run test --force`: agent-workflows 569 (568 passed, 1 skipped), api 200, web 243, agent-engine 326 (317 passed, 9 skipped) — all green, and the counts in features.md match what I measured. Three findings: the ending's gate holds while a loop is going round again (so `to decide` appears and an approval is accepted mid-round and later merges unasked), the brief a `--no-worktree` run hands its ending step is false, and `--gate <last step>` on a folder with no `ship.md` now loses the ship-it/drop-it commands.

findings.what: Nothing keeps two runs' ending steps out of the same checkout. `validate` refuses a second ending inside one workflow, but `workspaceFor` hands `run.repo` to any approved ending, and `tick` advances every run in one pass: approve two finished `dev` runs (the board's `to decide` list invites exactly that) and the next pass files both `ship` tasks with `cwd` = the repository, and the engine runs both at once (pool cap 2 by default). Both sessions read `git status --porcelain` as clean, both run `git merge --no-ff --no-commit`, and the loser's `git merge --abort` (step 5 of its own prose) throws away the winner's staged trial merge while the winner's `npm test` is running against it — two opus sessions wasted and the person's checkout rewritten under them. The only thing standing in the way is ship.md's prose, and the house rule is that the machinery refuses the alternative. A level-triggered refusal to file an ending while another run has one unsettled in the same repo (the store's other runs are already read for `forgetRefusal`) is the shape; there is no test for two runs at all.

The ending step gets the standard artifacts contract, whose second bullet is false for it and invites damage: "Or leave it in this workspace, and name it in `artifacts` by its path from the workspace root … the run copies each such file into that directory … A file left in the workspace is committed with the rest too." For a `workspace: main` step "this workspace" is the person's checkout, and `handOffDue` (run.ts:1132) now excludes the step, so `collectArtifacts` (runner.ts:1546) never runs and nothing is committed. A ship session that writes `merge-log.md` beside its closeout, as its brief tells it to, leaves an untracked file in the person's checkout for ever — and the next run's ship step then reads `git status --porcelain` as non-empty and signs off blocked at step 1 of its prose. It also contradicts ship.md's own "leave the checkout as you found it". Give a main-workspace step a contract with only the absolute-path bullet.

The send-back refusal at an ending's gate names the wrong step's gate and a command that is itself refused. On the shipped `dev` folders, `wf retry <run> review` (no --message) at ship's gate reaches the `sendsBack` branch added at run.ts:1317 and prints "review is awaiting approval: a try of it sends it back from its gate … — or approve it: wf approve <run> review." review is not awaiting approval (`wf ls` shows it `unverified · done`, ship `awaiting approval`), and `wf approve <run> review` is refused by `approvalRefusal` with "review has no gate … <run> is gated at ship." It should say ship is the step at its gate and name `wf approve <run> ship`. The test at test/run.test.ts:3320 does not catch it: `/^review is awaiting approval|--message/` is an alternation, so it passes whatever the sentence says.

`decision` does not apply `unheld`, so `wf decide` and the board contradict `wf ls` in the window the round-3 fix was meant to close. Between `wf retry <run> review --message "…"` and the pass that files it, `standing` still reads ship as `awaiting approval`: `wf decide` prints "AWAITING APPROVAL, waiting on you: ship — your approval is what runs it" and `gateLines` prints `wf approve <run> ship`, while `wf ls` (which does apply `unheld`) shows ship `waiting` with nothing to decide, and `wf approve <run> ship` is refused with "try 2 of review is asked for … approving now would take the result that ask objects to." The api's run page reads `decision` and `gateLines` too, so its Approve button is live in the same window. `decision` should take the same `unheld` adjustment `assess` and `listing` take.

`wf retry <run> ship` at the ending's gate — the step `wf ls` names on the line above the send-back — falls through to the default "ship is awaiting approval, and there is nothing to try again." Before this change every `awaiting approval` step had modes (a step with no followers hit the first `sendsBack` clause), so this state is new and lands on a message that names no fix: it should point at `wf approve <run> ship` and `wf retry <run> <the work> --message`, as `sendBackTo` already computes.

`wf round <run> review` at an ending's gate is refused with "…its loop is over and there is nothing to go round again. What waits on it has been filed: wf ls <run>." Nothing has been filed — ship is unfiled and waiting for the person's approval, which is the whole state they are standing in. `roundAsk`'s gate check at run.ts:1903 only looks inside `loopSpan`, so the ending's gate is invisible to it; the sentence should say the run is at its ending's gate and name `wf approve` / the send-back.

The board now tells a person to merge by hand a branch whose run has an ending step waiting to merge it. `commandsOf` offers `ship it  git merge --no-ff <branch>` and `drop it  git branch -D …` for any awaiting decision with branches, and a `dev` run parked at ship's gate is one — while `wf decide` deliberately suppresses both for a folder that merges (cli.ts:889, `!merges(steps)`). Outside your package, so the fix is one line for the board run (pass `merges(steps)` the way the CLI does); at minimum it belongs in features.md's "What it leaves", which does not name it.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the whole change against §8 and ran the suite: `npm run typecheck` clean and `npx turbo run test --force` green at the claimed counts (agent-workflows 575/574+1 skipped, api 200, web 243, engine 326). The four asked-for items are there and genuinely tested — `workspace: main` with its refusals at parse and at load, the ending's gate held before the step is filed, `to decide` in both kinds, `wf decide`'s facts, and `ship.md` on the four dev folders with a real-git store test. Seven findings, none of which breaks the happy path: the two worth acting on before this is used in anger are that nothing stops two runs' ending steps working in the person's checkout at once, and that the ending step's brief still carries the artifacts contract telling it to leave files in that checkout for a run that collects and commits nothing there. The rest are refusal and screen messages that are wrong or unhelpful at the new gate.

findings.what: `parentCloseouts` still reads `terminalSteps(steps)` while `tipBranches`, `decision`, `resultBranches` and `parentOf` moved to `resultSteps`. For a child started `--after` a dev/dev-planned run, the terminal step is now `ship`, so `## From run <id>` in the child's root brief carries ship's summary ("merged wf/<id>/implement onto main, the check passed") and no declared fields, instead of review's summary and its declared `findings`/`again` — ship declares no `output:`. That is the whole of what a `wf plan` chain hands forward, and it now says nothing about the work. Read `resultSteps(steps)` there too.

`wf decide` returns at `if (decision.direct)` before the standings and the new `to decide` block, so on a run started `--no-worktree` (allowed: `fansOut` only refuses a folder that forks, and dev is a chain) parked at ship's gate the screen prints "worked directly on main; nothing to merge" and returns — the ending's prose and the `wf approve <run> ship` that files it appear nowhere, and the per-step section skips ship too (`if (!c && !check && !run.steps[name]?.taskId) continue`). The new decide.test.ts test dodges this by starting `isolate: false` and then hand-writing `record.steps.implement.branch` to a `wf/...` branch, which a real `--no-worktree` run never has. Print the to-decide block before the `direct` return (the standings are rightly skipped there: they would read "main is on main").

`resume:` beside `workspace: main` is accepted — `validateMainWorkspace` only refuses followers and a second ending — and `composeBrief` returns at `if (step.resume && !retry && !round)` before the `workspace === 'main'` section, so such an ending step is never told it is in the repository's checkout, never given the result branch or the `git log`/`git diff`, and never told the run commits nothing there. It also continues a session whose `cwd` was the worktree while being filed with `cwd: run.repo`. Refuse `resume:` with `workspace: main` at load (with a test that makes it refuse), or handle `main` in the resume branch.

`wf rm` on a run parked at its ending gate says "ship waits at its gate for your approval, and what waits on it is filed once it is approved" — but nothing waits on ship; approving files ship itself, which is the one thing this gate changed. The new test at test/run.test.ts:3402 asserts that sentence, so the wrong words are pinned. Word it off `run.steps[name].taskId` as `wf ls`, `wf decide` and `wf approve` now do.

The measured counts are wrong: `npx turbo run test --force` on this branch gives agent-workflows 567 (566 passed, 1 skipped), not 565 — commit 0d74403 added a test after the docs commit — and agent-engine 326, not 317 (the entry at line 2618 already says 326, and the engine is untouched). A Shipped note whose numbers a later run cannot reproduce is worse than no number.

"The board's builder drops `workspace:` until apps/web's own `WorkflowStepSpec` carries it" (and the same claim in RESPONSE.md) is not true: `draftOf` and `changed` in apps/web/src/lib/builder.ts spread the spec (`{ ...spec, ... }`), so the key rides through the round trip at runtime, and `saveWorkflow` posts it back; the api side is proven lossless by builder.test.ts. What is actually missing is the key on the web's mirrored type (and its `keyof WorkflowStepSpec` key-form union). Stated as data loss it sends the board run after a bug that is not there.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the eight commits against §8: `workspace: main` with its two load-time refusals, `approvedFirst`/`waitsAtGate` (the ending's gate held before the step is filed), `resultSteps`, `toDecide` in `assess`/`listing`/`wf ls`/`wf decide`, and `ship.md` on the four dev folders. The suite and typecheck are green (agent-workflows 567/566 pass/1 skip, api 200, web 243, engine 326), the refusals each have a test that makes them refuse on `err.message`, and ship.test.ts genuinely exercises the merge, the send-back and the abort against real git. Six findings: one behavioural regression the change introduced and did not notice (`parentCloseouts` still reads `terminalSteps`, so an `--after` child is handed the merge report instead of the work's conclusion), a `wf decide` hole on `--no-worktree` runs, an accepted-but-mishandled `resume:` + `workspace: main`, a refusal whose words are now false at an ending gate, and two stale claims in features.md.

findings.what: The movedAside path lays the whole group out again even when only an open card can pin it, and the non-strict `placeTogether` then lets `cap` give way, so a card no graph covered lands in a column left of nothing. Example: the triangle b after a, d after a and b (for instance B = api after A = schema, D = web after both), laid out fresh as a (0,0), b (1,0), d (2,0). A person opens b with a 3×1 span. Its graph covers d but not a, so a stays in step 1 and d is movedAside. Then `unput([a])` runs, and `placeTogether([a,d], false)` gets first = col(b)+1−1 = 1 and cap = col(b)−1−0 = 0. Because cap < first it ignores cap and searches columns 1..2. It puts a at (1,1) and d at (2,1). Now a sits directly below b, in b's own column, and the a→b edge runs backwards from a's right side to b's left side. Before this round, a stayed at (0,0) and d went to (2,1), so every edge pointed forward. The same happens for any group where the opened card's parent and child are also joined by a direct edge: the diamond with `d --after a` too, or a chain with a skip. The layering guarantee is the point of the round-one fix, but the new tests only cover the diamond, which has no such edge (its path top→side→bottom leaves room). A `backwards(at, after)` test over the opened triangle would fail today. One fix: when the relayout is infeasible (cap < first) and the down cards were not covered, keep them where they are and place only the loose cards.

reviews.summary: I checked implement's five round-two fixes against the diff; `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass. The Runs row, the picker's word, the step name beside a long chip, and reading `onYou` off `Wait` all hold, and `neverShips` still not being exported is reported for the person who decides. The new layering in `placeRuns` has one regression. I traced it by hand, because running a scratch test outside the workspace was refused. When a person opens a card that sits between a parent and a child that also wait on each other directly, the parent moves out from under nothing into the opened card's column, and its edge runs backwards. The old code kept that parent where it was.

findings.what: A card whose run is still waiting on other runs says it has started. The footer shows `${since} since it started` for every run in flight, timed from `createdAt`, so the diamond's bottom card reads "waiting on the-other-side-runs-e2e6" and then "2m 02s since it started" (factory-diamond-light/dark.png), though nothing of it is filed. That contradicts the edge into the same card, which `runEdges` draws dashed "to come" because no step is filed yet. A person reading the card can take a waiting run for one already working. The footer should say something like "waiting since …" when `run.waiting` is set.

reviews.summary: Last round's finding is fixed. The triangle now has a test, and a whole group is laid out again only when every edge still points right; otherwise the cards already placed stay put. I checked the api (`after`/`waiting` on list, detail and decision, and the 400/422/guard refusals), the start form's picker, the edges and legend, and the e2e against the brief, and read the Factory, refusal and waiting-run screenshots in both themes. `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass; one small wording issue remains, not worth a round. For whoever merges: the "What it leaves" section of packages/agent-workflows/docs/features.md (lines 647–654) still says the api carries no `after`. This step was told not to touch packages/, so that edit is the merger's.

findings.what: The parents-left-of-children layering only holds for a fresh layout. When a graph covers some cards of a joined group but not others, `joined` (line 193) only collects the unplaced ones, so the layering is worked out over a partial group. And `first` only keeps a card right of its placed parents, never left of its placed children. The e2e hits this, and its own photograph shows it (implement/factory-light.png). After Reset layout, FAKE's graph covers top, shipped and bottom but not running, so those three are re-placed as a straight row (top col0, shipped col1, bottom col2). Opening the neighbour's graph then moves running, which is placed alone with first = top's column + 1 and lands in col 3, right of bottom, which waits on it. The running→bottom edge then runs backwards under the cards. The same happens with a person's saved positions, which step 2 restores one card at a time. Fix: cap a lone card's column below its placed children, or re-place the whole joined group once any member moves. Add a `placeRuns` test that starts from `onFloor` with only one diamond card displaced; the current tests only lay out from empty.

On a card whose root says `waiting on <run>`, the chip gets `max-w-full` and the step name is the part that shrinks. The bottom card in factory-diamond-light.png and factory-diamond-dark.png shows the step as "i…" beside `waiting on the-other-side-runs-e2e6`. A longer id, or a `(cancelled)` or `(<branch> gone)` suffix, leaves no name at all. The card already carries the full word on its own `data-waiting` line, so the name should keep its width (`shrink-0`) and the chip should truncate instead.

The Runs row decides "waiting on you" from `run.waitingOnYou` alone. A run waiting on a cancelled, missing or gone parent has `waitingOnYou: []` and `waiting.onYou: true`, so its row never says it waits on you. runs-light.png shows 'Waits on a called-off run' with no amber line, while the Factory counts it among "3 waiting on you". The row should use `waitsOnYou(run)`, which the Factory already uses, so the two pages agree.

`runWord` calls any run that is not in flight and not cancelled "finished". The picker therefore labels 'Waits on a called-off run' as `finished` (start-refused-light.png), though it has never filed a step and never will without a person. `afterRefusal` accepts it as a parent: it is not cancelled and has no result branch to be gone. So a person who trusts the label starts a child that waits behind a run blocked for ever. It should say `waiting on you` for a run where `waitsOnYou(run)` is true, or show `waiting.word`.

`neverShips` is copied from run.ts, where it is not exported, and `onYou`, which drives `moving` and the Factory's in-flight split, rests on the copy. The brief said to stop and say so rather than re-derive what the package does not export. If the package gains a reason a parent never ships, `waitAdvice` will say "yours to resolve" while the api still reports the run as moving, in flight on the Factory. The api test copies the same rule, so it would not catch that. At least name the missing export in the closeout so a person can export `neverShips` from the package.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the change against 35920da. `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` both passed, and I read implement's e2e photographs in both themes. The api is sound: its `after`, `waiting`, `moving` and decision fields are held to the package's own `list` and `decide` by tests, the refusals are tested at shipped defaults, and the default Factory floor draws the diamond as a diamond. But the Factory photograph taken after graphs unfold shows the layering broken: a parent sits right of the run that waits on it. I also found smaller gaps: a waiting card cuts its step name to "i…", the Runs list and the start form's picker word a run blocked on a cancelled parent wrongly, and the api re-derives one package rule the package does not export.

Reviewed the gate-on-the-board change against 500e7a2. The api route calls the package's approve() behind the guard, and its refusals were each tested to refuse. `gates`, `gate`, `approve` and `onYou` are on the detail and the list. The web side (Gate beside the rendered closeout, Approved under the step, the banner's `approve plan` link, the card's need, the Runs row) does what was asked. Last round's finding is fixed: withGraph refuses a detail from an older api, gateOffered offers the gate only when `approve` has words, and the Runs row falls back to step names. Tests exist for all three. `npx turbo run test --force` and `npm run typecheck` pass, and the e2e's gate screenshots in light and dark (awaiting, refused, approved) show what the brief asks for. I found nothing worth another round.

findings.what: `atGate = step.approve !== null` is true when `approve` is `undefined`, which is what an api process started before this change sends. With such an api, every step's section on the run page draws the Gate — Approve and Send back — beside its closeout, and pressing Approve gets the old api's 404. At the same time, `NeedsBanner` (apps/web/src/components/Needs.tsx:25, `run.onYou.map`) throws on any run that waits on you, and the Runs row (apps/web/src/routes/runs.index.tsx:86, `run.onYou.length`) throws for such a run too. That takes the page down instead of saying to restart the api. `withGraph` (apps/web/src/lib/api.ts:842) exists for exactly this case: it names the fix, and it gained a check each time the detail gained a required field (graph, tries, said, timeline). This change adds `onYou`, `gates`, and each step's `approve` and `gate` without one. The fix: have `withGraph` refuse a detail without `onYou`, or a step without `approve`, in its usual 'restart the api' words; and use `Boolean(step.approve)` for `atGate` so a missing field never offers Approve. A unit test for the refusal belongs beside withGraph's existing ones.

reviews.summary: I read the whole diff against 500e7a2, then ran `npx turbo run test --force` (all 4 packages pass; the api has 173 tests, all passing) and `npm run typecheck` (clean). I also looked at the e2e screenshots in both themes: waiting at the gate, refused, approved, sent back, plus the Runs and Factory pages. The api route, `gates` and each step's `gate`, the need `approve plan`, the Gate component, the banner line, the Factory card and Runs row, and the e2e's refusal page (409) all do what was asked, and each refusal has a test that makes it refuse. One robustness gap is worth a short round: every new field is read without checking it's there, so a board served by an api process older than itself shows Approve on every signed-off step and crashes the banner.

findings.what: `presetOf` looks up a workflow name on a card among the api's own repository's workflows, whatever repository the card names; `inbox.tsx:275` never passes it `entry.repo`. Take the card `wf inbox add "Cache the views" --repo /code/other --workflow dev` writes (`workflow: dev`, `repo: /code/other`) while the api serves a repository that also has a `dev`. The start form preselects the api's `dev`, so Start sends `{workflow: 'dev', from: 'repo', card}`. `folderOf` resolves that to `<api repo>/workflows/dev`, and the run gets that folder on `/code/other`. `wf start <inbox>/<card>.md` would run `/code/other/workflows/dev` (`workflowFolder(card.workflow, inboxDir(), card.repo)`). So clicking Start as preset runs a different workflow than the card names, and all that shows it is the small 'from …' path under the button. The api already handles this when filing: `filingOf` writes the folder path for a card about another repository because "its name would be looked for where it is not". The start preset ignores the same rule. features.md's 'What it leaves' describes this preset, but that is no reason to pick the wrong workflow: when the card names a repository other than the api's (`GET /api/repository`), preselect nothing and show the `data-unlisted` note, saying which repository the name belongs to. The web tests only call `presetOf` without a repository, so nothing covers this case.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the whole change since aef14f0, looking hardest at round 2's two fixes. Both hold: a card's repo is now written without a trailing slash and similar, and a card whose file could not be removed keeps its `why` after the inbox is re-read. api tests (152), web tests (180) and typecheck all pass, and the new inbox screenshots look right in both themes. One bug is left: for a card about another repository, the start form picks the wrong workflow. It is small to fix, so I'm asking for one more round.

findings.what: The inbox list reloads only after a start succeeds. Say a card was dropped or started in a terminal after the page loaded, and Start is refused: 404 ("no card X in the inbox. Its cards are: …") or 409 (started as another run). The card stays listed with Start and Remove until the page reloads. The e2e's `inbox-refused` picture shows exactly this: the 404 text sits under the card it says is not there. Remove has the same gap (apps/web/src/routes/inbox.tsx:176): a 404 there leaves the card listed with the refusal. Small, and the refusal text is clear; reloading the inbox after a 404 or 409 as well would fix it.

reviews.summary: Round 3's fix is correct. `presetOf` now presets nothing when a card names a workflow by bare name but its `repo:` is a different repository than the api's. Trailing slashes are trimmed, and a card that names an absolute folder still gets that folder preset. Tests cover it: unit tests make it refuse, and an e2e page checks the hand-written case, with screenshots taken after the commit in both themes. With the turbo cache off, api 152/152 and web 181/181 pass; typecheck passes from cache. Everything else in the api routes, guard, page and e2e holds, and all that is left is one small stale-list case, not worth another round.

findings.what: `POST /api/inbox` saves `repo` exactly as sent, but `wf inbox add --repo` cleans the path first (`path.resolve`, cli.ts:451). Someone who types `/home/me/code/app/` with a trailing slash in the Repository box gets a card with `repo: /home/me/code/app/`. `startFromInbox` then records `run.repo` with the slash, and the board matches runs by exact string (StartRun.tsx:121). So that card's start form says 'No run on this repository to wait on', and the Workflows page never offers the new run as one to wait on. The same function already uses `path.resolve(about)` to decide whether to write the workflow by name (line 113) but saves the raw value. Fix: save `path.resolve(about)` when `about` is absolute; leave a relative path as sent so the package still refuses it. Add a test that files a path with a trailing slash and asserts the card's `repo:` has none.

When a card's run is written but its file cannot be removed, the api answers 201 with `removed: false` and `why`. `StartRun` shows `why` (`data-kept`), but its `onSuccess` also refetches the inbox (StartRun.tsx:41). The refetched entry has `startedAs = [id]`, so `startable` is false and `{starting && startable && <StartCard/>}` unmounts the form and the message within milliseconds. The person sees only the generic 'Started as …, and still here because its removal failed' line, never the error itself (e.g. EACCES). features.md says 'A card that stayed says why, and the page stays', which does not hold. Nothing tests this case: no api test reaches `removed: false`, and the web and e2e tests only parse the answer. Fix: keep the start form's result mounted after a start that did not remove the card (or show `why` on the card), and add a test that covers it.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the inbox's api routes, the /inbox page, the e2e and the docs against the brief. The api and web suites and typecheck pass (typecheck replayed from turbo's cache). I read the e2e's inbox screenshots in both themes. Everything the brief asked for is there. Refusals are tested to refuse, and the e2e takes back every write. Two small bugs are worth a round: the api saves a card's repository path exactly as typed, where `wf inbox add` cleans it first, and the reason a card could not be removed disappears as soon as the inbox refetches.

Round 2: both round-1 findings are fixed. Queueing or unqueueing from the board now keeps the card file's modified time: an api test fails without the restore, and the e2e checks list order, the time shown and the file. The cap line now reads `3 of 4 run slots taken`, which departs from the brief's example `2 of 4 runs in flight`; features.md says why. The stream-close fix for the flaky `say` page e2e is confined to following.ts and unit-tested. `npx turbo run test --force` passed in all 4 packages; typecheck was green but replayed from cache; I ran no build or e2e (forbidden). No new findings.

findings.what: Queueing or unqueueing a card moves it to the top of the Inbox page and changes the date it shows. `queueInInbox` writes the card to a hidden file and renames it over the card, so the file's mtime becomes now. `listInbox` reads `filedAt` from that mtime, and the page sorts by `filedAt`, newest first. Repro: on the seeded Inbox page, click Queue on `planned` (listed 3rd). It jumps to 1st under the cursor and shows the queue time as its date. Unqueue does the same again. The e2e misses both. It only queues the card just filed, which is already first. Its 409 test writes the card behind the page's back and then sets the old mtime back by hand (`fs.utimesSync`). `inbox-queue-refused-*.png` shows the jump: `Cache the engine's views…` is listed first with 12:06 AM. Fix: keep the card's mtime across the api's queue write (stat before, `utimesSync` after), or have the page order by something a queue doesn't change. Then test Queue and Unqueue on a card that is not the newest, and assert that the order and `filedAt` stay the same. If the package's `queueInInbox` should keep the mtime itself, note that in the closeout, since `packages/` is off-limits here.

The header puts two different counts, both called "in flight", side by side: `4 in flight · 7 finished · 4 waiting on you │ 3 of 4 runs in flight · 3 queued` (factory-light.png / factory-dark.png). The floor's count (4) equals the cap (4), so the floor looks full, while the cap's line says a slot is free. Only the hover explains that the cap does not count a run waiting on another run. A person watching why queued cards don't start sees two numbers that contradict each other. Word the cap's count so it can't be read as the same number, e.g. `3 of 4 run slots taken · 3 queued`, and update the e2e's expected text to match. Lower priority than the first finding.

reviews.summary: I reviewed all six commits against the base. `npx turbo run test --force` passes in all four packages (api 175) and `npm run typecheck` passes. I also looked at the Factory and Inbox screenshots in both themes. The api routes, the guard, the refusal statuses and `/api/ceilings` hold up, and `held` matches the package's `runSlots`. One bug: Queue and Unqueue move a card to the top of the Inbox page and change the date it shows, and the e2e can't catch it. Separately, the Factory header shows two different "in flight" counts side by side.

I found nothing that needs changing. The Runs page now lists runs in flight first and the rest below, newest first in each group, with ties broken by id. The runs in flight are the same ones the Factory counts. Each group has a heading that gives its count, its order and how many of its runs wait on you, which answers last round's finding. The full suite passes when run without the cache (183 web, 152 api, 455 workflows, 307 engine tests, none failing; the last two include some skipped tests). Typecheck passes, and both screenshots of the Runs page, light and dark, show the headings and the order.

findings.what: Nothing on the page shows where the running runs (`inFlightFirst`) end and the rest begin. Rows have no run-level status, only step chips, so the date column looks unsorted at that point. In implement's own screenshot (runs-light.png), the last running row is 'A run beside it' at 7:50:46 PM, and right below it comes 'What it cost' at 7:54:16 PM, which is newer. The top group's chips don't read as 'running' either: 'The diamond bottom' shows `waiting on the-other-side-runs-e2e6` and 'Blocked by the harness' shows `needs-human`. Meanwhile 'What it cost', which waits on you, sits lower down. Someone who asked for 'most recent first, running on top' will see a newer run below older ones and read it as a sort bug. Suggested fix: label the two groups with a small heading or divider (e.g. 'In flight' / 'Finished'), and have the e2e check that the boundary falls after the four running rows.

reviews.summary: The Runs page now lists runs that are still going first (`inFlightFirst`, using the Factory's `inFlight`), then all the others, each group newest first, with ties broken by id. I found no correctness bugs: the unit tests pass (41/41), typecheck passes, the e2e checks the order against the seeded store, and implement's screenshot `runs-light.png` shows the order the code intends. One finding, and I'm asking for a second round on it: nothing on the page marks where the running runs end, so at that point the dates look out of order.

findings.what: The comment on `claudeOps.say` says delivery was verified end to end by `test/live.test.ts` and points to `docs/open-issues.md` "verified live". That section has no `say` entry: it lists only `--tools`, the MCP fence and releasing a settled session. The run's artifacts have no live-test log either, only `implement/say-probe.md` and `implement/say-blocked-probe.log`, and neither mentions live.test or AE_LIVE. So nothing on the branch shows that `say` ever reached a live session. The README's "measured on 2.1.270 before relying on it" and this comment both rest on a claim that exists only in implement's closeout reply (passed twice on 2026-09-14, Claude Code 2.1.270, the second run seeing the words as an attachment line). Someone who follows the pointer before merging finds nothing. Last round asked for this run to be recorded, and implement's reply says it was not. Fix: add a 'Verified live, once' entry giving the date, the harness version, what the told and control sessions did, and which transcript shape arrived, or remove the pointer.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the `say` change against 4cf04e6 and ran the engine's tests without the cache (122 pass across say, decide, transcript, engine and readme; `npm test` and typecheck are green from turbo's cache). The code does what was asked: delivery before the journal entry, every refusal made to refuse with nothing sent or journalled, `decide` untouched, and last round's four fixes hold. One doc gap remains: a runner comment points to a live-run record that is not on the branch.

findings.what: `postLine`'s 5 s timeout rejects even after `written` is true. By then the line is in the socket buffer, and Claude Code reads it once its event loop gets to the connection. So when a session's process is stalled for more than 5 s, the session still gets the words, but `Engine.say` says `was not given the words (... took nothing within 5000 ms). Nothing was journalled.` That is delivery with no trace, the failure `say` exists to prevent, and a person who says it again sends it twice with one entry on the record. Fix: once `written`, a timeout while waiting for the inbox to close should resolve (the words were handed over), or reject with a message that says they may have arrived. No test covers this: add an inbox that reads the line and never closes.

The check that refuses a socket owned by another uid is only ever tested allowing. The one `uid` parameter feeds both the registration check and the socket check, so a test passing another uid (say.test.ts) is stopped by the registration check first and never reaches this line. CLAUDE.md requires every new refusal to be made to refuse. Fix: give the socket check its own uid parameter, or pull the checks on the socket's stat into a pure function a test can hand another uid, and test it refusing.

`say` accepts a session listed `blocked`, and README.md:715 and this comment state as fact that it reads the words once it moves again. The probe measured only a busy session and an idle one. A `--bg` session blocked on a permission prompt that nobody attaches to may never move. B8's board then continues it as a new attempt that never gets the words, while the journal says they were said to the old one. Either measure the blocked case live, or add it to open-issues.md as half-verified beside issue 12.

The transcript check passes on any event whose `text` contains the file name, including the model's own text such as 'Writing SAID-….txt'. So it can pass even if the new attachment reader (runner.ts, `queued_command` with a `peer` origin) is broken. Restrict it to `e.kind === 'system'` with the exact words. Separately, `engine.say` at line 254 is outside `settleThenCheck`'s try/finally, so a rejection there leaves both `--bg` sessions running and registered. Also, open-issues.md records no run of this test, yet runner.ts:913 cites `test/live.test.ts` as the measurement; the measurement was the hand probe (artifacts/implement/say-probe.md). Run it with AE_LIVE=1 and record the result, or cite the probe instead.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the `say` change in agent-engine. It works: engine suite 259 pass, 0 fail, 5 live tests skipped; agent-workflows 339 pass; typecheck clean. It posts the words to the session's own Unix inbox socket and journals `said` afterwards. The refusals, the `decide` pin and the old-journal fold are all tested. There are two correctness gaps worth a round: a slow inbox makes a delivered message look undelivered, and the socket-owner check has never been made to refuse. Two claims also rest on no measurement: the live test's own transcript check and what a blocked session does with the words.

findings.what: `textAfterSaid` empties the box only when it still holds exactly the words sent, and otherwise keeps everything, including those words. Case: a person types "Widen it.", presses Enter, and keeps typing " And the api" while the POST is pending. The box is left holding "Widen it. And the api". Pressing Send again hands the session "Widen it." a second time. The engine journals it twice, and `wf decide` and the next try's `## Said to your session` show it twice. `apps/web/test/say.test.ts` asserts this as intended ('typed on after sending'). Keeping only what was typed after the sent words (`now.startsWith(sent) ? now.slice(sent.length).trimStart() : now`) would keep the new text without resending the old.

reviews.summary: Both round-1 fixes hold. `heardIn` now draws words said to a session once. Its two arrival shapes (a working session's `queued_command` line and an idle session's isMeta line) match what the engine's transcript reader actually emits. The box also keeps text typed while a send is in flight. `npm run typecheck` passes and `npm test` has no failures (engine 262 of 267 pass with 0 failing, workflows 348 of 349 with 0 failing, api 114, web 158); I did not run build or e2e, but I read the implement step's say-said and say-refused screenshots in both themes and they look right. One small finding is left for a person, not worth another round: the new keep-typed-text rule can make a person send the same words twice.

findings.what: In a real session, the words a person says appear twice on the session page. When Claude Code takes the words, the engine's transcript emits them as an event of their own: a `kind: 'system'` event whose text is the words, for a working session (agent-engine/src/runner.ts:343), or an `isMeta` line with Claude Code's wrapper around them, for an idle one. `foldTranscript` draws either as a system marker (transcript.ts:103-105), and `withSaid` keeps that marker and adds a "You said, while it ran" bubble from the journal. So saying "Widen the scope to apps/api too." to a running step shows the sentence as an info marker, or inside the fold of calls around it, and again as the bubble right after it. The e2e's seeded `draft` conversation (seed.ts `draftConversation`) never writes the `queued_command` attachment a real delivery does, so the check that the turn is on the page cannot see the duplicate. Fix: drop or restyle the arrival event that matches a `said` entry (same text, just before its `at`). Also seed that attachment line in the e2e, so the page is checked the way a real session renders it.

`onSuccess` always calls `setText('')`, but the textarea stays enabled while the POST is pending. That POST observes `claude agents` twice (once in `say()`'s `e.view`, once inside `Engine.say`) and writes to a socket, so it takes a noticeable moment. Someone who sends one message and starts typing the next before the 202 comes back loses what they typed. Clear the box only if it still holds the words that were sent, e.g. `setText((now) => (now === words ? '' : now))` using the mutation's variables, or disable the field while `send.isPending`.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the whole change against 7762c46: `wf say` and `sayRefusal`, `saidLines` in `wf decide`, the `wf ls` note, `## Said to your session` on nudges and rounds, the guarded say route, and the session page's prompt box. `npm test` passes in all four packages, `npm run typecheck` passes, and I read implement's say/session screenshots in both themes. The package and api parts do what was asked and test every required refusal at shipped defaults. Two findings on the session page: in a real session the words show twice, which the e2e never sees, and the box erases text typed while a send is in flight.

findings.what: `wf decide <supervisor run>` floods the question it exists to show, and worsens with every merge. A one-step `workspace: main` workflow is a shape nothing had before: `resultSteps` returns [] for it (run.ts:775, the step's own `after` is empty), so `decision.branches` is empty and `branchesToRead([], ...)` falls back to "every branch a step worked on" — which for this run is `run.branch` itself, since `workspaceFor`'s `main` case records the base branch. So `touchedBy(run, 'master')` diffs `<baseRef>...master`, and `baseRef` is frozen at `wf start` while master advances with every run the supervisor approves. The screen then prints, ABOVE the closeout and the `needs` the person came to read: `touched master` with its radius; a `lesson` line crediting the supervisor with whatever CLAUDE.md/docs edits other runs merged; and `inFullLines`' complete diff of every CHECK_AFFECTING path merged since — `**/*.test.*`, `**/test/`, `**/package.json`, `**/package-lock.json` — which for one merged dev run is already thousands of lines. Day one it is `touched master — nothing`, which is what docs/features.md:2965 records as "honest, and not useful"; day two it is not nothing, and the claim is wrong. `tipBranches` (run.ts:787) already refuses exactly this case with `branches.includes(run.branch) ? []`; the decide screen has no such rule — and it must stay for a `--no-worktree` run, whose fallback branch really is its work, so the signal is `run.isolate` (true here, false there). Nothing tests `wf decide` on a run whose only step works in the checkout.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the supervisor folder, `slot: none`, the `workspace: main` brief changes and the `taskPhases` gate against the code they touch; suite and typecheck are green (agent-workflows 586, 4/4 packages). The slot exemption, its refusals and the never-ending path hold up, and the round-1 findings are genuinely answered — the `earlierTries` gate in particular is safe, since every reader of an earlier try's cost returns before it without a cap in force. One defect left: `wf decide` on a supervisor run — the way both READMEs tell a person to read its question — falls back to diffing the base branch, so it prints every merge made since the run started, in full for check-affecting files, above the question.

findings.what: The new brief for a `workspace: main` step whose run has no result branch ends with "The checkout is at `<run.baseRef>`" — a present-tense claim about the checkout, made from the sha frozen at `wf start`. `baseRef` is only ever rewritten for a run with `--after`, and the supervisor's run never ends in the one checkout every other run's `ship.md` merges into. From the first merge onwards every recomposed brief (one per answer, dozens over a day) names a commit several merges behind, and a session that acts on it — `git diff <baseRef>`, `git log <baseRef>..HEAD` — reads other runs' merges as the state it is responsible for: the same mistake round 3 removed from `wf decide`. The other sentence in the block, `results` "cut from `<baseRef>`", is a historical fact and stays true; only this one goes false. Nothing tests it: run.test.ts:295 asserts the sentence is present, not that what it says is still so on try 30. Say the base branch by name, or read HEAD where the brief is composed, or drop the clause.

"**Never type git for a run.** Not `git merge`, not `git branch -D`, not a push, not a checkout of its branch" is the most consequential rule in the brief and is enforced by nothing — against CLAUDE.md's *Prose is not a constraint*, and with no test that makes it refuse. The step works in the person's real checkout with the base branch checked out and has every tool but the four on line 14, so a `git merge <run branch>` lands work on main that no ending step trial-merged and no person approved; a `git checkout <run branch>` leaves the checkout off the base and stops the next `ship.md` at its step 1. `.claude/settings.json` already denies `Bash(git push:*)` and `Bash(git branch -D:*)`, so those two are real; it cannot deny `git merge` because `ship.md` runs in the same checkout and needs it — which makes this step's own `disallow:` (line 14) the only place the refusal can live. Either add the denies with a test that makes one refuse, or say in the folder's README why prose is the best available guard here.

"What it leaves" says of the board only that "a run that never ends is drawn as any other ... nothing says 'this one is the supervisor'". It is worse than that on the operator's first day: a step that signed off `blocked` is in `stopsFollowers`, so `assess` gives the run `failed`, and `RunStatus` on the board is `'running' | 'succeeded' | 'failed' | 'cancelled'` — the supervisor's normal, healthy, waiting-for-you state draws its card as a failed run for as long as it waits. `wf ls` is unaffected (its run line carries no status word), so the gap is the board's alone. One sentence in this bullet would keep the operator from reading the first question it asks as a crash.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the whole diff against the brief: the `supervisor` folder and its README, `slot: none` through the parser, `validate` and all three cap readers, the `taskPhases` earlier-tries gate, the `branchesToRead` base drop, the artifacts contract split, and the new tests. Ran `npx turbo run test --force` (agent-workflows 587 / 586 pass 1 skip, api 202, web and engine unchanged) and `npm run typecheck` — all green. I traced every consumer of `views` inside `advance` and every path to `spendOf` to satisfy myself the earlier-tries gate loses nothing, and confirmed the CLI's `wf decide` never reaches the fallback with a base branch for a run that cut worktrees. Three findings, none a machinery bug: a present-tense claim in the new brief that goes stale, the git prohibition left to prose where `disallow:` is available, and a board state the Shipped section undersells.

findings.what: The supervisor is told it may write CLAUDE.md / features.md / plan-hold-the-bar.md in the repository's own checkout, and is given no rule about when. `workflows/dev/ship.md:21-23` — which runs in that same checkout — says `git status --porcelain` must say nothing, and otherwise signs off `blocked` with "somebody else is working in this checkout". So the sequence the brief actively encourages (diagnose a stall → "write it down" → `wf approve <run> ship`) leaves an uncommitted file in the tree for exactly the tick that files the approved ship, and the ship refuses. Worse when the supervisor writes a file and then signs off `blocked` to ask a question: the tree stays dirty for as long as the person takes to answer, which is the window an earlier yes's ship gets filed in. The brief covers the opposite direction (line 110: don't touch a checkout mid-merge) but not this one. It needs "commit what you wrote, by path, before any `wf approve`, and never sign off with the checkout dirty". Related: the recipe given is `git commit <path>`, which fails on a path git does not yet track, and the brief forbids `git add -A` without offering `git add <path>`.

"It still takes a session slot, like every session (`WF_MAX_CONCURRENT`)" understates the cost at shipped defaults. `ceilings()` (runner.ts:361) defaults `sessions` to 2, counted per harness pool; `supervise.md` is `harness: claude`, and so are `dev`'s implement, review and ship. The supervisor's loop is `wf ls` → `sleep 60` → `wf ls`, so its session is *running* nearly all the time and holds one of the two `claude` slots continuously — it only frees one in the gap between signing off `blocked` and being answered. The operator who starts the first run therefore drops the board from two concurrent claude sessions to one, and `slot: none` (which exempts it from `WF_MAX_RUNS`) does nothing about it. Neither the README, supervise.md nor features.md's "What it leaves" says this, so the first symptom is a board that has mysteriously halved. It wants a sentence naming the default of 2 and the recommendation to raise `WF_MAX_CONCURRENT` before starting the supervisor.

`taskPhases` reads `e.view` for every earlier try of every step, on every pass, with no cache across passes — and `advance`, `list`, `decide` and `runSlots` each call it. For every other workflow the try count is bounded by `retries:` and a person's patience; the supervisor is the first step designed to be answered without limit, and each answer appends a try (the new test asserts `tries.length === 5` after five). So the supervisor's run costs N+1 journal reads per `wf up` tick (every 4000ms) and per `wf ls`, growing linearly and for ever: ~100 reads/tick after a hundred answers, ~500 after five hundred, plus a run record whose `tries` array is rewritten each pass and a `timeline` the board renders over all of them. features.md's "Nothing caps a step answered many times, and there was nothing to lift" answers the question §9 asked about a *cap*, but this is the thing the package actually lacks for a step that never ends, and it is neither measured nor listed under "What it leaves". The lever is visible: earlier tries' views are read to total `stepSpend` against `budget:`, and `supervise.md` sets no `budget:` — so for this step every one of those reads buys nothing.

"**The step is told both ways**, on its brief, beside the closeout contract (`artifactsContract`): put a file in `<dir>` and name it by absolute path, or leave it in the workspace and name it by its path from the workspace root." This is no longer true after the `artifactsContract(dir, inMain)` change: a `workspace: main` step is now told exactly one way, and `run.test.ts` asserts the brief does *not* contain "Or leave it in this workspace". A reader of this section — or the next agent writing an ending step — would tell a `workspace: main` step to leave a file in the workspace and have it silently not collected. The same sentence is in docs/features.md:1128. The README gained a supervisor section but this bullet was not amended.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the supervisor change: `slot: none` through the parser, `validate`, `slotNeed`/`runAdmitted`/`takesNoSlot` and the pass's count, the `workflows/supervisor/` folder, the `workspace: main` brief fixes, and the tests. Suite and typecheck are green and the slot machinery is correct and honestly tested — every caller updated, refusals tested on `err.message` at shipped defaults, and the never-ending path exercised on disk. Four findings, all about how the session behaves once the operator actually starts it: it can block the very `ship` it approves, it silently halves the `claude` session pool, its per-pass cost grows with every answer, and one README bullet is now untrue.

findings.what: The inner component is typed `P & { onClick?: unknown }`, and TanStack takes a link's props from that component, so `<NavLink onClick={picked}>` (last round's code) still compiles. At run time `routeLink` throws the handler away: on a phone, picking a place would leave the menu open, with no error. No link passes `onClick` today and the comment warns about it. Typing it `onClick?: never` would make typecheck reject it (CLAUDE.md: 'Prose is not a constraint').

reviews.summary: Round 2 review: all three findings from the last round are fixed, and I checked each against React Aria's code. `routeLink` drops TanStack's click handler, so React Aria makes no extra click on keyup and the provider navigates once; the new Enter check in the e2e is sound; the menu is a list again and is documented as a local edit. The web app's 234 unit tests pass run directly and typecheck shows no errors (the root `npm test` was a turbo cache replay); `build` and `e2e` are not allowed in this step, so I read the implement step's screenshots instead. One small trap is left for a person, not worth another round.

findings.what: Nothing tests the `RouterProvider` that `__root.tsx:37` adds. Remove it and Enter on a sidebar place (Runs, say) reloads the whole page again, with every check still green, because the e2e only clicks links. Why: pressing Enter on a focused `<a>` makes the browser fire a click, and React Aria does not stop it. `usePress`'s onClick ignores a keyboard press (usePress.mjs:290), and `handleLinkClick` does nothing without a provider (openLink.mjs:147), so the browser follows the link. CLAUDE.md now asks for a check by hand instead. A check that fails without the provider: set a marker on `window`, focus a place's link, press Enter, wait for the URL, then assert the marker is still there and `history.length` grew by one.

This trap, the comment at `apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:35` and features.md:2702 all say Enter makes a click that 'never reaches the router's `onClick`'. That is wrong. The router's `onClick`, and `picked` merged into it, does run on Enter, but on keyup through `triggerSyntheticClick` (usePress.mjs:311). By then the browser's own click from keydown has already started a full page load. With the provider in place, Enter now navigates twice: once through React Aria's `router.open` on keydown, then through TanStack's `onClick` on keyup. The second goes to the same URL, so TanStack calls `router.load()` again (router-core router.js:408) and the loaders run twice. Someone who trusts the current wording could conclude that `onClick={picked}` never runs on Enter and move it, or look for the bug in the wrong place. Say what actually happens: the browser's click from keydown is not prevented, and the router's handler only runs on keyup.

`SidebarMenu` and `SidebarMenuItem` changed from `ul`/`li` to `div`/`div`. A screen reader no longer announces the main nav as a list of five places. features.md:2734 puts this under 'what the base does not offer', but React Aria plays no part in it: the aria-nova registry just ships `div`s. Putting back `ul`/`li` (and the `React.ComponentProps` types) is a two-line local edit, like `showCloseButton={false}`, not a workaround of the base. Either restore the list and note it as a local edit, or move this out of the base's limits and call it the registry's markup, kept on purpose.

reviews.summary: The switch to shadcn's `aria-nova` base holds up. `npx turbo run test --force` passes in all four packages (web 234/234) and typecheck is green. I read React Aria 1.21.1's own code: the Show finished switch's `id` lands on its input, links, modal and folds behave as the app expects, and the sidebar matches the registry's aria-nova file. The implement step's screenshots look right in both themes. Three findings: the RouterProvider fix for Enter on a menu link has no test; the docs and a code comment give the wrong reason for that bug; and the nav lost its list semantics, which the docs blame on the base when it is only the registry's markup.

findings.what: `versionOf` skips hidden files (`!e.name.startsWith('.')`), but the package treats a hidden `.md` as a step. `loadWorkflows`' `stepFiles` lists it, and `writeWorkflow` (runner.ts:1062) removes every `.md` file that is not the README and not in the draft, hidden ones included. So if someone adds `.notes.md` to a folder of yours while the builder has it open, the version does not change, Save gets a 200, and the file is deleted without warning. That is the lost update this round's 409 was meant to stop. Fix: count every `.md` that `writeWorkflow` would remove, hidden or not.

The test writes `.draft.md`, asserts the version does not move ('a hidden file'), then at line 473 saves `[plan, build]` and expects a 200. That save deletes `.draft.md` (writeWorkflow removes it), and the test never checks the file is still there. So it passes while encoding the data loss above. Once the version counts hidden `.md` files, this case should expect a 409 with `.draft.md` kept. A hidden non-`.md` file (e.g. `.notes.txt`) can stay as the case that leaves the version alone.

reviews.summary: Round 2 review: the three fixes hold up. Schemas now go in the same PUT as the steps and are checked with them before anything is written. The stale-save check (409) works, with Read the folder again on the board, and the raw control bytes are gone, with a test in each app that refuses them. The suite passes (api 190, web 225, forced turbo run), typecheck is clean, and the builder-changed and builder-saved screenshots look right. One hole remains in the new version check: a hidden `.md` added by hand is not counted in the version, yet the save deletes it, and a test runs exactly that save without noticing.

findings.what: The loop that writes the pasted schemas runs before the `try`, so only a `writeWorkflow` failure puts schemas back. A failure while writing a schema does not. Example: `a.schema.json` is new and `b.schema.json` is read-only on disk. `a.schema.json` gets written, writing `b.schema.json` throws EACCES, and the route returns 500 with `a.schema.json` left in the folder. No step names it, and the folder's version has changed. features.md (§ The board half, 'or the disk fail, each schema is put back as it was') promises otherwise. The 500 test only covers a failure inside `writeWorkflow`.

The banner says 'Not saved, and nothing written' for every error, including a 500 and a failed fetch. Neither guarantees that. `writeWorkflow` writes the step files one at a time, so on a disk failure partway (for example `[build, plan]` with `plan.md` a folder, EISDIR) `build.md` is already written. The api puts back only the schemas, and the board still says nothing was written. The same goes for a fetch cut off after the api wrote. Only a 4xx is known to have written nothing, so a 500 or a network error should say the folder may have been written and suggest reading it again.

reviews.summary: Round 3 review. Both of last round's findings are fixed. `versionOf` now counts hidden `.md` and `.json` files, and the test expects a 409 that keeps the file for `.draft.md` and `.shared.schema.json`, and checks that a note and a subfolder survive a save. With turbo's cache off (`--force`), `npm test` passed in all 4 packages and `npm run typecheck` passed. The e2e screenshots taken after the last commit (saved, refused, changed; light and dark) show the builder working. Two small gaps are left, both on the disk-failure path: a person should see them, but they aren't worth another round.

findings.what: Save writes each pasted schema (PUT …/schemas/:file) before it puts the folder, and the schema PUT only judges the text against the steps already on disk (`judgedWith`, apps/api/src/builder.ts:318). A schema pasted for a new `output:` is named by no step on disk, so any JSON object (`{"type":"object"}`, or a non-strict one) is written with a 200. The folder PUT is then refused by the parser, and the board says "Not saved, and nothing written" (line 187). The file stays in the folder after Discard and is offered in the schema select on the next listing. The same happens when a paste replaces an existing schema and the draft is refused for something unrelated, like a cycle: the file is overwritten and the save refused. Neither the web unit tests nor the e2e exercise the pasted-schema save, so none of this is caught. Judge the pasted schema against the draft before any write (for example, send it with the folder PUT and parse with a `read` override, as `judgedWith` does), or at least say what was written.

The control-character classes in `workflowNameRefusal` (line 172) and `schemaNameRefusal` (line 184) are raw NUL, 0x1F and DEL bytes in the source, not `�-` as the package writes them. Because of the NUL, ripgrep treats builder.ts as binary: a search of `apps/api/src` for `judgedWith` or even `import` returns nothing for this file (checked), and searching the file directly stops with "binary file matches (found \0 byte around offset 11847)". Every later step or person searching the api misses the builder, and a reader sees the class as `[ -]`. Write the escapes.

The PUT writes whatever draft it is sent, with no check that the folder is still what the draft started from, and the builder never re-reads it (`base` is fixed at open, WorkflowBuilder.tsx:63). While the builder is open on `mine`, add `ship.md` by hand, or change `plan.md`'s check in an editor or another tab; then change any key on the board and Save. `writeWorkflow` deletes `ship.md` (shown only afterwards as "removed") and rewrites `plan.md` from the stale draft, silently undoing the edit. That is the read-modify-write lost update CLAUDE.md's one-writer rule warns about. Have the PUT carry what the draft was read from (the listed steps, or a digest of the files) and refuse with a 409 and a reload sentence when the folder no longer reads as it.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the builder change: the api's three writes, the board's builder and the e2e do what §4 asks, and `npx turbo run test --force` (api 186, web 223, packages unchanged) and `npm run typecheck` are green. Three findings: Save's pasted-schema path writes a schema file before a folder PUT that can be refused and then says nothing was written (with no test of that path); builder.ts holds raw NUL/control bytes that make ripgrep treat it as binary; and Save overwrites or deletes changes made to the folder since the builder opened, with no conflict check.

findings.what: Stale files are removed only after every step's file is written, and a name counts as stale unless it matches exactly. On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS, or a repo on /mnt/c under WSL), renaming step `Review` to `review` goes wrong. `put('review.md')` reads or writes the existing `Review.md` entry. Then `Review.md` is not in `names`, so `rmSync` deletes that one file. The step's body is lost, the other steps' `after: review` now name no step, so the folder no longer loads, and the returned `steps` say it does. Removing stale files before writing, or comparing names case-folded, would fix it.

`e.isFile()` on a readdir Dirent is false for a symlink, but `loadWorkflows` reads a symlinked `old.md` as a step. If a folder has a symlinked step file that the save drops, the file is never removed. The folder then still reads that step, even though `steps` in the result leave it out. If that step waits on a step the save removed, the folder no longer loads, though the write reported success. And for a symlinked step file the save keeps, `fs.writeFileSync` (line 1052) writes through the link into whatever file it points at. Nobody links step files today (the api only documents linked folders), so this is low priority. It is still a gap in the promise that the folder reads back as the steps returned.

reviews.summary: The change does what the request asked, and `npx turbo run test --force` passes: 543 tests in agent-workflows, 1 skipped (a live test skipped before this change too), and 166 in the api. `npm run typecheck` passed as well, though turbo replayed a cached result for it. `renderStep` round-trips every shipped folder. `writeWorkflow` parses the whole folder in memory before it writes anything and checks where it writes, and every new refusal has a test that asserts the folder is unchanged. I found two edge cases in how `writeWorkflow` removes files. Neither is reachable on the Linux (ext4) setup this runs on today, so neither is worth another round.

findings.what: `viewOf` observes through the composite `Runner` (line 386) whenever the task's harness has no `find`, settled or not. The composite's `observe` runs every harness, `claude agents --all --json` included. agent-workflows' `check` harness (a HarnessSpec) and `codex` have no `find`, so every `view` of a check or codex task still costs about 330 ms. The api's polled run detail views each step's check task (apps/api/src/app.ts:1006 → :372), and so does every `wf` pass (agent-workflows/src/runner.ts:277). A run with checks keeps paying one `claude agents` call per check per poll after every check has settled. Observing only the task's own harness (`runners[harnessOf(state)].observe`), as `transcript` already does, gives the same view for that task without the Claude registry. Separately, README.md:801-802 says 'a list of runs asks the registry only for the steps still running'. The api's list already read one `e.list()` before this change (everyView, app.ts:693, :1298), and a run's detail still asks the registry for each check task.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the four commits on 08bef91 (items 16, 17 and 18, and the round-1 fixes) against decide, engine, facade, runner and the upstream callers of `view`. `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` are green (turbo cache replays). I found no correctness bugs, and both round-1 replies hold. One finding: a `view` of a task whose harness has no `find` (check or codex) still runs `claude agents`, and README.md:801 claims more saving than there is.

findings.what: Two guards in `claudeRegistered` have no test that makes them refuse, though CLAUDE.md requires one and the commit says every guard was taken out once and a test failed. (a) `!stat.isFile()`: `find.test.ts` only ever writes regular files. Remove the check and a symlinked `<pid>.json` is followed and taken, with no test failing. (b) line 587, `typeof r.sessionId !== 'string' || !r.sessionId`: every registration the test writes has a string `sessionId`. Remove it and a registration with `"sessionId": ""` comes back from `find` as `{ sessionId: '' }`. `transcript` of the running attempt then takes `''` (it is not nullish for `??`) and returns no events for as long as the attempt runs, instead of observing. Needs a test each: a symlinked registration, and one with a missing or empty `sessionId`, both not found.

Says a run now sees a quiet-without-closeout step `failed` rather than `unsigned`, and 'both are final, and both are offered a nudge and a fresh try'. It leaves out three changes. The run's outcome goes from `blocked` to `failed` (agent-workflows/src/run.ts:1625). The step drops out of `wf ls`'s 'waiting on you', which lists `unsigned` but not `failed` (run.ts:1726). A nudged retry is told 'The last try's session ended `failed` before it signed off' (run.ts:1919) instead of being told it gave no closeout. The comment at run.ts:345 ('The engine settles a session `succeeded` when it ends…') is now false. The engine side is what item 18 asked for and agent-workflows is out of this step's scope, so the note should say all of this, so the merger or plan carries the follow-up instead of reading the two statuses as equivalent.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the three agent-engine commits (resume.test usage assertion, `find`, and quiet without a closeout now ending `unsigned`) against the ask. Suite and typecheck are green, and the logic in `decide`, `viewOf` and `transcript` matches the ask. Two findings: two guards in `find` that no test makes refuse, and an open-issues note that understates how agent-workflows now reports a step that went quiet without its closeout.

findings.what: This change adds a new state: an ask for a step that is still running. It is only due on a pass where the engine says `needs-human` (`blockedByHarness`). Case: `wf retry r implement` on a harness-blocked step, then the session starts working again before any tick stops it. §4b records that the operator unblocked sessions by cross-session message on 2026-09-13, and with no `wf up` running the window lasts until the next tick. From then on the ask is not due and `wf ls` shows no note. It is also never spent: `spentAsks` needs `tryOf >= 2`, and the step stays on try 1. If the step later ends failed, stopped or unsigned, or its check refuses, the next pass files try 2 from that old ask at once. The ask branch in `retriesDue` also runs ahead of `retries:`, so nobody is asked again. A task with no `stopRequested` tells this stale ask apart from one whose stop is under way. The tick could honour it by stopping the session anyway, or `wf ls`/`wf decide` could name it; no test covers this.

reviews.summary: I reviewed the change against 35920da; all three items do what was asked. Typecheck is green, and `npm test` passed with turbo replaying cached results for this tree: 322 pass and 1 skip in workflows, 98 in api, 126 in web, 235 pass and 4 skip in engine. The new store tests would fail on the old code. I checked the engine end to end: a stop only appends to the journal and cannot throw, and claude-bg still lists a stopped session, so the stopped task keeps its session id and the nudge resumes it. The api's `decision` call compiles unchanged and picks up the shipped fix. One thing for a person: `retry()` accepts a harness-blocked step only when the caller opts in, and only the CLI does, so the board's POST still answers 409 for such a step until apps changes. `features.md` documents this and the edits apps needs. One low-severity edge follows, not worth another round.

findings.what: The 'two tasks filed at the same instant are admitted in the order of their ids' test passes even with the id tiebreak deleted from `admissionOrder` (engine.ts:282). `Journal.test()` (and facade.test's memoryJournal) return `list` already sorted and Array.prototype.sort is stable, so equal times keep id order without the comparator's third clause. The tiebreak only matters for a PromiseJournal whose `list` is unsorted — the README's own example (`db.job.findMany()`) is one — and nothing tests that case: a journal listing ids in reverse would.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the three commits: priority-then-filing-order admission in tick, `priority` refused unless finite and shown in `ae ls`, and `remoteControl` passed as `--remote-control` before `--permission-mode` and refused on every harness built like a check. The full suite passed with the cache forced off, and typecheck passed as replayed from cache. Nothing needs another round; one small gap: the equal-times test can't tell whether the id tiebreak exists.

findings.what: Text outside the engine that this change made wrong, which the brief kept the implementer from fixing: (1) `wf --help` still says `WF_MAX_CONCURRENT  sessions per harness at once (default 2)`. After this branch the setting counts sessions at work per pool, so someone reading it would expect 2 `claude` plus 2 `claude-detached` sessions, or a blocked session to take a slot. (2) The comments at `apps/api/src/app.ts:439` ("Each `view` observes every harness — a `claude agents` call"), `:209` and `:618` say a `logs` or `view` call observes every harness again. That was the reason for not reading earlier tries' check output, and it's no longer true: a check's `logs` now only reads the check harness's own run files. (3) `packages/agent-workflows/docs/features.md` still describes, as current (§3 'What exists', around line 1898), that a blocked session holds its slot and that `claude` and `claude-detached` are counted apart, and still lists both as work the engine has to do ('Engine-side work', around lines 1925–1931). And `docs/plan-hold-the-bar.md` item 27 (lines 1070, 1077) is still open. Whoever merges should update these.

No test covers the `h === 'claude-bg' ? CLAUDE_POOL` branch of `poolsOf`. The only test that sets up `'claude-bg'` registers it under the name `claude` (`test/pool.test.ts:120`). There, the fallback `h.pool ?? name` also gives `claude`, so deleting the branch leaves every test green. The case that would break is the one `HarnessConfig`'s doc promises ('whatever either is called'): a map like `{ cc: 'claude-bg', 'claude-detached': claudeDetached }`.
