Without the branch, `cc` and `claude-detached` would be counted as two pools, and a ceiling of 2 would again let four Claude Code sessions run. A single pass with `'claude-bg'` under another name would pin it down.

reviews.summary: I found no correctness bugs, and all three items are done as asked, one commit each. A view now asks only its task's own harness, and falls back the way `harnessOf` does. The ceiling counts only `working` sessions, and each tick counts them again from scratch. Pools are declared on the harness: `claude-bg` and `claudeDetached` share `claude`'s pool, and `codex` and `check` each have their own. The tests the brief asked for exist, and each fails if its change is undone. I ran six of the engine's test files directly (pool, engine, find, readme, decide, facade: 127 pass, none fail); the root `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` came back green but from turbo's cache, not a fresh run. One file outside the engine changed: `apps/api/test/asks.test.ts` now expects 4 `claude agents` calls instead of 5. That count had to change once item 1 landed, and it's still an exact count (nothing loosened); the commit message explains it. The two findings below are for whoever merges, not worth another round.

findings.what: The api never reads `permissions.ask`. Claude Code's docs say an ask rule makes one of the read-only commands ask, and in dontAsk anything that asks is denied. So a repository whose `.claude/settings.json` has `ask: ["Bash(cat:*)"]` gets a Capabilities page that shows `cat` solid under "Claude Code's read-only commands do not ask" on a dontAsk step, and that step's `cat` is denied. This is the reverse of the claim item 30 set out to remove. The gap is written down only in commit 0fba515's body, in no doc a person reads (not features.md, not the plan). Either handle `ask` rules the way deny rules are handled for those commands, or record the gap where the page's other open items live.

This test checks the dated `READ_ONLY_COMMANDS.measured` list against the repository's current `.claude/settings.json`. Suppose someone later adds `Bash(ls:*)` or `Bash(cat:*)` to `permissions.allow`, which is a harmless change. `npm test` then fails, and the failure says the 2026-09-15 measurement is wrong and should be demoted. It isn't wrong: it was taken under the settings of that day. The guard is only meaningful when someone edits the data, and it will break for an unrelated settings change. Pin the allow list the measurement ran under inside the test or the data, rather than reading the live file.

reviews.summary: I read all three commits against the brief and found no correctness bugs. `npx turbo run test --force` passes in all 4 packages, and `npm run typecheck` passes (a cached result for the same inputs). I didn't run build or e2e, since they write into the workspace; I read the screenshots the implement step's e2e wrote instead, and the refused inbox, remove-refused, conflict and capabilities pages look right in both themes. I checked the read-only command list against Claude Code's permissions docs and it matches. Two small items are worth a person's attention but not another round: `permissions.ask` is still not read, and one api test ties a dated measurement to the live settings file.

findings.what: The new note says what an ask rule covers — "a read-only command, an allow, a server's tool" — is "struck on a dontAsk step". A server's tool is not: in capabilities.tsx:326 a dontAsk tool with `asks` and no deny gets ASKS (amber), the same chip as any tool no rule allows, and only its title says "Asks by …". A reader of the doc expecting `mcp__fixture__echo` under `ask:` to be struck on a dontAsk step finds it amber. Either word the note as "marked asking, and denied on a dontAsk step", or strike the tool chip when `tool.asks` is set in dontAsk.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the four commits against 6886203. Both findings are fixed and tested: ask rules are read, cover read-only commands, allows and server tools, and are denied and struck on dontAsk steps; the read-only list is pinned by shape and date, with a guard proven to refuse. Last round's two fixes hold. Api 161 and web 191 tests pass (forced), typecheck is clean (from turbo's cache), and both theme PNGs show the page right. One small docs inaccuracy, not worth a round.

findings.what: The list of narrower ask rules under a standing allow (`narrowerDenies(rule, asked)`, here and at line 251 for `allowed.bash`) keeps ask rules that a deny already covers. With allow `mcp__fixture`, deny `mcp__fixture__wipe` and ask `[mcp__fixture__echo, mcp__fixture__wipe]`, a step not in dontAsk shows "except mcp__fixture__wipe and asks for mcp__fixture__echo, mcp__fixture__wipe", but wipe is denied and never prompts. Bash does the same: allow `Bash(npx turbo run test:*)` with `Bash(npx turbo run test build)` in both deny and ask reads "except X and asks for X". The test at apps/api/test/capabilities.test.ts:713 expects `asks: ['mcp__fixture__echo', 'mcp__fixture__wipe']`, although its title says "a deny of it comes first" and its tools row gives wipe `asks: null`. Drop from `asks` any ask rule a deny covers (for MCP, `denyingRule(deny, server, tool)`; for Bash, a deny whose scope covers the ask rule's scope), and fix the test to expect `asks: ['mcp__fixture__echo']`.

Deny rules get a repository-level "Denied" section with a count; ask rules get nothing at that level and show only inside a Claude Code step. A repository whose settings have `ask: ["Bash(cat:*)"]` and whose workflows are all Codex, or which has none, never shows its ask rules on the page, although the api returns `asked`. The brief asked for ask rules to be shown the way deny rules are. The e2e's own screenshots show "Denied 3" and nothing for Bash(cat:*) at repository level. Add an Asks section beside Denied, with its count and an empty-state sentence, plus an e2e line for it.

reviews.summary: Both findings are fixed, and `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass. The api reads permissions.ask in the order Claude Code's docs give (deny, then ask, then allow), marks a covered read-only command as asking and denies it on a dontAsk step. The page strikes it and says why, and the dated list now has a check that refuses a missing day, version or source, while a settings file that allows ls passes. Two small gaps remain: under an allow, a rule a deny already refuses is also listed as asking, and a test expects that; and ask rules have no repository-level section the way deny rules do.

I found nothing worth changing in either commit. Priority: the first filing of a step with no `after` has no priority, and every other filing has priority 1: steps that wait on another, tries, rounds and checks. Those are the only four places the package files a task. `remote:` is accepted only as `true` or `false` and is carried as `remoteControl` on every session filing, never on a check. `remote: true` on codex or claude-detached is refused at start before anything is written, including through `wf plan` and inbox starts. That refusal uses the same harness rule as the engine, and a test asks the real engine for its wording. `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass from the root. I reran agent-workflows (527 pass, 1 skipped: the paid live test) and api (166 pass) with `--force`, because turbo had replayed cached results. The board's workflow list still shows a codex workflow with `remote: true` as valid, since only start refuses it. The brief asked for exactly that.
